items.title: Windows update fails: locked .pyd files by running python/pythonw processes

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description

Every time Hermes Desktop attempts to update on Windows, the updater fails because running Hermes processes (gateway, TUI workers, Desktop app) have `.pyd` and `.exe` files locked in the venv. The user has to manually end-task all python/pythonw processes via Task Manager before clicking "Retry install" — every single time.

## Error Messages (alternating between these two)

**Error 1:**
> INSTALL DIDN'T FINISH
> "Hermes is still running. Close all Hermes windows and try the update again."

**Error 2:**
> INSTALL DIDN'T FINISH
> "Cannot remove item C:\Users\ADMIN\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent\venv\Lib\site-packages\tornado\speedups.pyd: Access to the path 'speedups.pyd' is denied."

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have Hermes Desktop running with gateway active (normal usage)
2. When an update is available, click to update (or `hermes update`)
3. Update fails with one of the above errors
4. Must manually: End Task all python.exe + pythonw.exe processes → Retry install

## Root Cause

Windows file locking. The updater (`hermes-setup.exe`) does not stop Hermes processes before attempting to replace files in the venv. These processes have `.pyd` native extensions loaded:

- `python.exe` — gateway (`hermes_cli.main serve`)
- `python.exe` — TUI slash workers (`tui_gateway.slash_worker`)
- `pythonw.exe` — background gateway process
- `Hermes.exe` — Desktop app + Electron subprocesses (GPU, renderer, network, audio)

## Environment

- OS: Windows 10
- Hermes: v0.18.0 (2026.7.1)
- Install path: `C:\Users\ADMIN\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent\`

## Suggested Fixes (pick one or combine)

### Option A: Pre-update process management (recommended)
The updater should detect and gracefully stop all Hermes-related processes before replacing files. Use `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process` with command-line matching (`*hermes_cli.main*`, `*hermes-agent*venv*`, `*tui_gateway*`) to identify exactly which processes belong to this Hermes installation, then stop them.

### Option B: Windows Restart Manager API
Register with [Restart Manager](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/rstmgr/restart-manager-portal) — it can shut down processes that hold locks on specific files, let the installer proceed, then restart them.

### Option C: Atomic rename strategy
Instead of deleting+creating files in-place, rename the old files to a temp location first (Windows allows renaming locked files), then place new files. Clean up old files on next reboot via `MoveFileEx` with `MOVEFILE_DELAY_UNTIL_REBOOT`.

### Option D: Update before process start
If the Desktop app is the entry point, have it check for updates and apply them *before* spawning the gateway/TUI worker processes. This way no venv files are locked when the updater runs.

## Current Workaround

Users must manually open Task Manager → End all python.exe/pythonw.exe/Hermes.exe processes → Click "Retry install". This is error-prone and frustrating for non-technical users.

labels.description: Web dashboard / control panel UI (dashboard/, landing)

items.body:
## Problem

`GET /api/actions/{name}/status` tails maintenance action logs for dashboard polling, but the shared `_tail_lines()` helper in `hermes_cli/web_server.py` used `Path.read_text()` before slicing the last requested lines.

That means every dashboard poll for actions such as `hermes-update`, `gateway-restart`, `doctor`, `security-audit`, `backup`, `import`, `skills-install`, or `tools-post-setup` loads the entire per-action log into memory even though the endpoint returns at most 2,000 lines.

## Why this matters

Long-running or noisy maintenance actions can leave large append-only logs under `~/.hermes/logs`. While an operator keeps the dashboard open, the browser repeatedly polls the status endpoint, so a large log turns into repeated full-file reads and transient allocations. This can make the dashboard unnecessarily expensive exactly while a recovery/update operation is being monitored.

## Evidence

Source path:

- `hermes_cli/web_server.py::_tail_lines()` read the full file with `path.read_text(...)`.
- `hermes_cli/web_server.py::get_action_status()` calls that helper for `/api/actions/{name}/status` after only clamping the requested line count.

Duplicate check:

- Existing PR #27273 is for `hermes logs` filtered tail expansion in `hermes_cli/logs.py`, not dashboard action status logs.
- Existing issue #25916 is broader durable action lifecycle work; it does not fix the current full-file action log read.
- Searches for `dashboard action status log tail read whole file` and `action log tail dashboard status` did not find an exact report or fix.

## Expected behavior

The dashboard status endpoint should read only a bounded tail window from the action log while still returning the requested recent lines.

## Validation from the proposed fix

- `uv run --extra dev python -m py_compile hermes_cli\web_server.py tests\hermes_cli\test_web_server.py`
- `uv run --extra dev pytest tests\hermes_cli\test_web_server.py -k action_status -q` -> `3 passed, 339 deselected`

items.title: bug(profiles): profile export default fails on Docker/custom HERMES_HOME with broken symlinks

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Describe the bug

`hermes profile export default` crashes with `shutil.Error` when `HERMES_HOME` points outside `~/.hermes` (common in Docker deployments) and the directory tree contains broken symlinks (e.g. stale symlinks in an unrelated `x11-dev/` directory).

## To Reproduce

Set up a Docker/custom deployment where `HERMES_HOME=/opt/data` (also the cwd) with a directory like `x11-dev/` containing stale symlinks:

```bash
HERMES_HOME=/opt/data hermes profile export default -o /tmp/test.tar.gz
```

## Expected behavior

Creates a clean archive of profile data (skills, config, cron, scripts, sessions).

## Actual behavior

```
shutil.Error: [("/opt/data/x11-dev/usr/lib/.../libXi.so", ..., "[Errno 2] No such file or directory")]
```

## Root cause

1. `export_profile("default")` calls `shutil.copytree(HERMES_HOME, ...)`. When `HERMES_HOME` is the cwd (Docker), this copies the **entire** working directory — not just Hermes artifacts. The blocklist (`_DEFAULT_EXPORT_EXCLUDE_ROOT`) can't anticipate every non-Hermes file.

2. `shutil.copytree(symlinks=False)` follows symlinks and crashes on broken ones. Should be `symlinks=True`.

## Suggested fix

Replace the blocklist with an **allowlist** of known Hermes profile directories (skills, cron, scripts, sessions, config.yaml, SOUL.md, etc.) so only actual profile data is exported.

## Related

- #5022: same class of bug (copytree too broad, fixed with blocklist)
- #3963: previous default-profile export fix

items.title: multiplex_profiles: per-profile display settings ignored, always read from root config

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description

When `multiplex_profiles: true` is enabled, per-profile `display` settings (e.g. `tool_progress`, `interim_assistant_messages`, `streaming`) are **ignored**. The gateway always reads `display` from the root/main `config.yaml`, regardless of which profile is processing the request.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable `multiplex_profiles: true` (top-level in root config.yaml)
2. Create a secondary profile with its own `config.yaml` containing:
   ```yaml
   display:
     tool_progress: false
     interim_assistant_messages: false
   ```
3. Root config has:
   ```yaml
   display:
     tool_progress: all
     interim_assistant_messages: true
   ```
4. Send a message to the secondary profile's adapter
5. Observe: tool progress and interim messages are still delivered, using root config settings

## Expected Behavior

Per-profile `display` settings should be respected. If a profile sets `tool_progress: false`, no tool progress messages should be generated when that profile processes a request.

## Actual Behavior

`tool_progress` and `interim_assistant_messages` from the root config are used for ALL profiles under multiplex. Per-profile overrides are silently dropped.

## Likely Cause

`_resolve_gateway_display_bool()` in `gateway/run.py` receives `user_config` that is always the root config object. Under multiplex, it should resolve the active profile's config instead.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent installed via pip, running under systemd
- multiplex_profiles: true
- Two Telegram adapters with separate bot tokens
- Linux server

## Impact

Profiles cannot independently control display noise. A profile that should be silent (no tool progress, no streaming) inherits the root profile's verbose settings.

items.title: /new doesn't reset model config — old session keeps using stale model after config change

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## What happened

改了 `config.yaml` 里的模型之后（从 `deepseek-v4-pro` 换到 `mimo-v2.5-free`），旧 session 还在用老模型。发 `/new` 以为重置了，但其实没有。

两边平台都试了：
- **元宝**：`/new` 之后恢复正常，新 session 用了新配置 ✅
- **QQ**：`/new` 之后还是老模型，401 报错，最后靠 fallback 才跑起来 ❌

同一个 `/new`，结果不一样。

## 复现

1. config 里配好 provider A + model B，跑起来
2. 在 QQ 上聊天，session 存下来了
3. 改 config 为 provider C + model D
4. QQ 上发 `/new`
5. 再发消息 — 还是用的 model B，不是 model D

## 日志

QQ 这边，`/new` 在00:20处理了，但00:56跑的时候还是老模型：

```
00:56:59 session turn: model=deepseek-chat provider=deepseek
00:57:01 API call failed: 401 Model deepseek-chat is not supported
```

重启 gateway 之后 session 从 storage 加载回来，老模型又回来了：

```
01:25:11 session turn: model=deepseek-chat provider=deepseek  ← 还是老的
01:25:13 Fallback activated: deepseek-chat → mimo-v2.5 (opencode-go)
```

元宝那边，`/new` 之前也报了同样的401，`/new` 之后就正常了：

```
01:09:51 session turn: model=deepseek-chat provider=deepseek  ← 老的，401
01:09:55 /new received
01:23:49 session turn: model=mimo-v2.5-free provider=opencode-zen  ← 新的，正常
```

## 配置变更

```yaml
# 之前:
model:
  default: deepseek-v4-pro
  provider: deepseek
  base_url: https://api.deepseek.com/v1

# 改成:
model:
  default: mimo-v2.5-free
  provider: deepseek
  base_url: https://opencode.ai/zen/v1
```

## 猜测

session store 里缓存了 `model` 和 `provider`，`/new` 重建 session 的时候没有从当前 config 读，而是用了 storage 里存的旧值。gateway 重启后又从 `state.db` 加载回来，老模型就一直跟着。

日志里有这行：

```
Stored system prompt for session has stale runtime identity; 
rebuilding for model=deepseek-chat provider=deepseek
```

看起来 session reset 路径没有完全清掉 model/provider 的元数据。

## 期望

`/new` 之后应该用 `config.yaml` 里当前的 `model.default` 和 `model.provider`，不是 storage 里缓存的旧值。

## 环境

- Hermes Agent: latest (post-`047b48d`)
- 平台: QQ Bot, Yuanbao
- OS: Windows 10

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop chat sessions are tagged as TUI and receive terminal guidance

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Bug Description

Desktop chat sessions are routed through `tui_gateway`, which unconditionally stamps sessions and agents as `platform="tui"`. The desktop chat panel is a graphical chat surface, not a terminal UI, so the agent receives terminal-specific platform guidance while running in the desktop app.

This can make the agent suggest TUI/CLI-only slash commands to a desktop chat user instead of using desktop-appropriate guidance.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Launch the Hermes desktop app.
2. Start a new desktop chat session.
3. Ask about a workflow that touches MCP/tool reload behavior.
4. Inspect the session metadata/system prompt, or observe the agent suggesting terminal/TUI-only slash commands as chat actions.

## Expected Behavior

Desktop chat sessions should be tagged as a desktop chat surface. The system prompt should describe the desktop renderer's actual capabilities: graphical chat, rich Markdown rendering, MEDIA:/path file handling, and inline image rendering.

Standalone `hermes --tui` sessions and `hermes --tui` launched inside the desktop's embedded terminal pane should still be tagged as TUI.

## Actual Behavior

Desktop chat sessions are tagged as `source=tui` / `platform="tui"` because `tui_gateway` is shared by the TUI and desktop backend. The system prompt then includes terminal UI guidance for a graphical desktop chat session.

## Affected Component

- Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)
- Other: Electron desktop chat / tui_gateway session creation

## Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (desktop chat surface)

## Debug Report

No paste debug report is attached. This is reproducible by inspecting the desktop session created through `hermes serve` / `tui_gateway` and by exercising the env-var matrix in tests.

## Operating System

macOS

## Python Version

Python 3.11.15

## Hermes Version

Hermes Agent v0.18.0

## Additional Logs / Traceback

N/A

## Root Cause Analysis

`tui_gateway/server.py` hardcodes `platform="tui"` when constructing `AIAgent`, and defaults the session DB `source` field to `tui`. The desktop app's chat backend reuses `tui_gateway`, so desktop chat sessions inherit the TUI tag even though `HERMES_DESKTOP=1` already distinguishes the desktop chat backend from standalone TUI sessions.

`HERMES_DESKTOP_TERMINAL=1` is separately set only for shells launched in the desktop's embedded terminal pane, which should remain TUI.

## Proposed Fix

Resolve the platform/source tag from the existing env-var matrix:

- `HERMES_DESKTOP=1` and `HERMES_DESKTOP_TERMINAL` unset => `desktop`
- `HERMES_DESKTOP_TERMINAL=1` => `tui`
- neither set => `tui`

Add `PLATFORM_HINTS["desktop"]` for the desktop chat surface and remove the separate desktop runtime hint from environment hints so the platform hint is the single source of truth.

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: [Bug]: Anthropic OAuth setup-token tests fail on macOS keychain subprocess path

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Bug Description

`tests/agent/test_anthropic_adapter.py::TestRunOauthSetupToken` fails on macOS because the tests patch `subprocess.run` globally to stub the `claude setup-token` invocation, but `run_oauth_setup_token()` then calls `read_claude_code_credentials()`, which also uses `subprocess.run` on macOS to read Claude Code credentials from Keychain.

The Keychain reader receives the `MagicMock` returned by the test's global subprocess mock and later passes it into JSON parsing, producing:

```text
TypeError: the JSON object must be str, bytes or bytearray, not MagicMock
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run on macOS.
2. From a dev checkout, run:

```bash
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_anthropic_adapter.py
```

## Expected Behavior

The `run_oauth_setup_token()` tests should pass on macOS and should only stub the intended `claude setup-token` subprocess invocation.

## Actual Behavior

Three tests fail:

```text
FAILED tests/agent/test_anthropic_adapter.py::TestRunOauthSetupToken::test_returns_token_from_credential_files
FAILED tests/agent/test_anthropic_adapter.py::TestRunOauthSetupToken::test_returns_token_from_env_var
FAILED tests/agent/test_anthropic_adapter.py::TestRunOauthSetupToken::test_returns_none_when_no_creds_found
```

The failure occurs because the macOS Keychain subprocess path receives a `MagicMock` instead of real subprocess output.

## Affected Component

- Developer experience (tests, docs, CI)

## Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A

## Debug Report

N/A. This is a local unit-test isolation issue.

## Operating System

macOS

## Python Version

Python 3.11.15

## Hermes Version

Hermes Agent v0.18.0

## Additional Logs / Traceback

```text
TypeError: the JSON object must be str, bytes or bytearray, not MagicMock
```

## Root Cause Analysis

`run_oauth_setup_token()` in `agent/anthropic_adapter.py` runs `subprocess.run([claude_path, "setup-token"])`, then calls `read_claude_code_credentials()`.

The tests patch `subprocess.run` globally. On macOS, `read_claude_code_credentials()` calls the Keychain reader, which also uses `subprocess.run` to invoke the `security` command. Because the global mock is still active, the Keychain code receives a `MagicMock` and attempts to parse it as JSON.

## Proposed Fix

Narrow the test mock so only the `claude setup-token` subprocess call is stubbed, while the Keychain credential reader is either:

- mocked directly, or
- bypassed through a patched `_read_claude_code_credentials_from_keychain()` returning `None`.

This keeps the tests platform-stable and avoids exercising macOS Keychain subprocess behavior under a generic subprocess mock.

items.title: [Bug] cron scheduler.py run_job() never reads per-job max_tokens — AIAgent() always gets None

labels.name: sweeper:not-planned
labels.description: Sweeper: closed per standing maintainer policy (design direction)

items.body:
## Summary

`cron/scheduler.py`'s `run_job()` never reads a scheduled job's own `max_tokens` config key. A job can set `"max_tokens": 4096` (or any value) in its `jobs.json` entry and it is silently ignored — the `AIAgent(...)` constructor call in `run_job()` never passes `max_tokens=`, so it always defaults to `None`, regardless of what the job config says.

## Root Cause

`AIAgent.__init__` (in `run_agent.py`) accepts a `max_tokens: int = None` parameter. `agent_init.py` assigns it directly to `agent.max_tokens` (line ~460), and it's later read by `chat_completion_helpers.build_api_kwargs()` — the function that constructs every primary per-turn request — which reads `agent.max_tokens` at several call sites across its provider branches. There's also a documented global fallback (`agent_init.py` ~line 1265) that reads `model.max_tokens` from `config.yaml` when the per-instance value is `None`.

So the plumbing exists everywhere except the one place that would let a **per-job** override reach it. In `cron/scheduler.py`, `run_job()` reads several other job-config keys directly into the `AIAgent(...)` constructor call (`job.get("model")`, reasoning config, prefill messages, toolsets, etc.) — but `job.get("max_tokens")` is never referenced anywhere in the file (confirmed via `grep -n "max_tokens" cron/scheduler.py` returning zero hits before the fix below).

## Impact

Any cron job whose expected output is longer than the model's default max-output behavior fails with `RuntimeError: Response remained truncated after 3 continuation attempts` after exhausting the continuation-retry loop — and setting `max_tokens` in that job's own config to try to fix it does nothing, silently. This can also mask the *actual* root cause of a truncation (e.g. #43900's num_ctx issue) since a user reasonably tries the documented per-job knob first, sees no effect, and has no signal that the knob was never wired up at all.

## Repro

1. Create a cron job whose prompt/output regularly exceeds ~2K tokens, pointed at any `custom`/Ollama-backed model.
2. Add `"max_tokens": 8192` (or higher) directly to that job's entry in `~/.hermes/cron/jobs.json`.
3. Trigger the job (`hermes cron run <id>`) and observe: identical truncation behavior with or without the key present. No error, no warning — the key is just inert.

## Fix

One-line addition in `cron/scheduler.py`, right after `model = job.get("model") or ...`:

```python
job_max_tokens = job.get("max_tokens")
```

...then pass it into the existing `AIAgent(...)` call:

```python
agent = AIAgent(
    model=model,
    ...
    max_tokens=job_max_tokens,
    ...
)
```

**Verification:** traced the fix through source — `job_max_tokens` → `AIAgent(max_tokens=...)` → `agent_init.py` (`agent.max_tokens = max_tokens`) → `chat_completion_helpers.build_api_kwargs()`, which reads `agent.max_tokens` directly into the primary request kwargs across its provider branches. Then confirmed behaviorally, not just by source-reading: set a job's `max_tokens` to a distinctive test value, enabled `HERMES_DUMP_REQUESTS=1`, triggered the job, and inspected the actual outgoing request body written by the dump — `max_tokens` was present with the exact test value, byte-for-byte, in the real HTTP payload sent to the model endpoint. Job also completed without error, confirming no regression.

## Related

- #21498 — same *class* of bug (silently-dropped max-tokens config), but a different code path: that one is about `config.yaml`'s provider-level `max_output_tokens` key being dropped by `hermes_cli/config.py`'s normalizer. This issue is about the cron-job-level `max_tokens` key in `jobs.json` never being read at all — no normalizer involved, just a missing `job.get()` call in `run_job()`.
- #43900 — a *different* root cause that produces the identical symptom (truncation after 3 continuation attempts): Ollama's `num_ctx` defaulting to 4096 and never being forwarded by the OpenAI-compat route. Worth checking both if you hit this error on a cron job.

items.title: [Bug]: Codex app-server can time out after completed assistant text

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Summary

When the optional Codex app-server runtime receives a completed `agentMessage` item but the subprocess never emits `turn/completed`, Hermes keeps waiting until the outer turn deadline. At the deadline it issues `turn/interrupt`, marks the turn interrupted/partial, retires the session, and surfaces a timeout state even though a complete assistant message was already projected.

## Affected path

- `agent/transports/codex_app_server_session.py::CodexAppServerSession.run_turn`
- Runtime mode: `model.openai_runtime = codex_app_server`

## Expected behavior

If Hermes has already received a completed non-empty assistant message and no error or explicit interrupt occurred, the turn result should keep that text as the terminal response instead of converting it into a timeout/partial result solely because `turn/completed` was omitted.

## Actual behavior

`run_turn()` only sets `turn_complete` on `turn/completed` or raw `<turn_aborted>` markers. A completed assistant item sets `result.final_text`, but if no later `turn/completed` arrives the deadline block still runs and flips the result to interrupted with a timeout error.

## Proof

A focused regression test using the existing fake Codex client queues only:

- `item/completed` with `item.type = agentMessage` and text `done`
- no `turn/completed`

Before the fix this path reaches the timeout branch and requests `turn/interrupt`; after the fix it returns `final_text == done`, `interrupted is False`, `error is None`, and does not retire the session.

## Duplicate search

Searched open and closed PRs/issues for:

- `codex app-server missing turn completed final response`
- `codex app-server turn completed timeout assistant`
- `turn/completed codex final_text`
- `turn timed out after codex final_text`

I found older Codex Responses stream issues such as #32883 / #32892 / #32908, but not the app-server session path where `agentMessage` completed while `turn/completed` was missing.

### Bug Description

In a **unified (multi-profile) dashboard** — one `hermes dashboard` process serving several profiles via the SPA profile switcher — the **gateway / platform status badge is never re-scoped to the selected profile**. It always reflects the machine-level / default profile's platforms.

The backend already supports per-profile status: `GET /api/status?profile=<name>` returns the correct per-profile `gateway_platforms` (verified working). The **frontend never sends the `?profile=` param** for the status call, so switching the SPA profile selector changes Sessions/Config/etc. but leaves the status badge showing the default profile.

Concretely: a WhatsApp-only secondary profile whose gateway is genuinely **connected** shows **WhatsApp: "Disabled"** on the dashboard, no matter which profile is selected in the switcher.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run two profiles on one host, each with its own gateway on a different platform — e.g. `default` (Telegram) and a second profile `faustina` (WhatsApp-only, enabled via its profile `.env`). Both gateways connected.
2. Start a single unified dashboard: `hermes dashboard` (no `--isolated`).
3. In the SPA, use the profile switcher to select `faustina`.
4. Look at the gateway/platform status badge.
5. For comparison, hit the backend directly (endpoint is public, no auth):
   ```
   curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:9119/api/status'                 # -> gateway_platforms: {"telegram":{"state":"connected"}}
   curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:9119/api/status?profile=faustina' # -> gateway_platforms: {"whatsapp":{"state":"connected"}}
   ```

### Expected Behavior

After selecting `faustina` in the switcher, the status badge should reflect **that profile's** platforms — WhatsApp shown as **Connected** — by fetching `/api/status?profile=faustina`, the same way Sessions/Config/Keys were scoped in #26066.

The `/api/status` handler's own docstring already promises this:
> "Plain /api/status stays the machine-level public liveness probe. The dashboard adds `?profile=` when its management switcher targets another profile, so its gateway badge reflects the selected profile."

### Actual Behavior

The badge always shows the **default/machine profile**. The selected profile's platforms are shown as **"Disabled"** (any platform not present in the default profile's `gateway_platforms`). The switcher has no effect on the status badge.

`curl /api/status?profile=faustina` proves the backend returns the correct, live per-profile state — so this is purely a frontend wiring gap.

### Affected Component

Web dashboard (SPA status/gateway badge). Backend `/api/status` is correct.

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

Surfaces on WhatsApp here, but the bug is platform-agnostic — it affects any non-default profile's status badge.

### Operating System

Linux (Raspberry Pi OS, `6.12.62+rpt-rpi-v8`, aarch64)

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

v0.18.0 (2026.7.1) · upstream 26dca5e5

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

- **Backend is fine.** `GET /api/status` (`hermes_cli/web_server.py`) accepts `profile=`, enters `_config_profile_scope(profile)` (the `set_hermes_home_override` ContextVar from #26066), loads that profile's config via `gateway/config.py::get_connected_platforms()`, and filters the live `gateway_state.json` `platforms` accordingly. Manually requesting `?profile=faustina` returns `{"whatsapp":{"state":"connected"}}` with a fresh `gateway_updated_at`.
- **Frontend never passes the param.** In the dashboard API client, `getStatus()` is hardcoded to `/api/status` — every StatusPage call site invokes it with no argument, and the shared fetch helper injects only the session-token header, never a profile. In the built bundle this is visible as:
  ```js
  // hermes_cli/web_dist/assets/index-*.js
  getStatus:()=>q(`/api/status`)                                  // no ?profile=
  function bf(e){return e?`?profile=${encodeURIComponent(e)}`:``} // helper exists…
  function xf(e,t){…`profile=${encodeURIComponent(t)}`}           // …but not applied to getStatus
  ```
  The `?profile=` append helpers (`bf`/`xf`) already exist and are used for other endpoints — they're just not wired into the status call. So the handler's documented "management switcher adds `?profile=`" contract is unfulfilled for the status badge.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Thread the currently-selected profile into the status fetch: have the dashboard API client's `getStatus()` accept the active profile and append `?profile=<name>` (reuse the existing `xf`/`bf` helper), and have the StatusPage poller pass the switcher's selected profile — mirroring the pattern #26066 established for the sessions/config/env endpoints. Omitting the profile (default selection) should preserve today's machine-level behavior exactly.

Related: #26066 (added `?profile=` scoping for Sessions/Config/Keys — status badge appears to have been missed on the frontend), #44035.

_Workaround for operators today: run a profile-scoped dashboard — `hermes --profile <name> dashboard --isolated --port <other>` — whose plain `/api/status` resolves to that profile's home, so its badge is correct._

items.title: [Bug]: MoA _collect_stream drops tool_calls in quiet mode — aggregator tool-call responses cause empty_response_exhausted crash

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Bug Description

In **quiet mode** (kanban workers, subagents, `hermes -z`), the MoA `_collect_stream` function (`agent/moa_loop.py:184-224`) collects only `delta.content` and `delta.reasoning_content` from the aggregator's streamed response — it **does not collect `delta.tool_calls`** and hardcodes `tool_calls = None` on the fake response message.

When the aggregator model (acting model) decides to call a tool instead of producing text, its streamed response contains `tool_calls` deltas but **no `content`**. `_collect_stream` discards the `tool_calls`, producing an empty `_FakeMessage` (`content=""`, `tool_calls=None`). The conversation loop then detects `_truly_empty` (no content after stripping think blocks), retries 3×, and crashes with `empty_response_exhausted`.

## Reproduction

**Environment**: Hermes v0.18.0, custom OpenAI-compatible MaaS provider (adapter-ca, `maas-glm-5.2-aliyun`), MoA preset with 3 reference models + 1 aggregator.

**Minimal repro** — call the MoA facade directly with `tools` parameter:

```python
from agent.moa_loop import MoAChatCompletions

facade = MoAChatCompletions("default")
response = facade.create(
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "Read the file /tmp/test.txt"},
    ],
    tools=[{"type": "function", "function": {
        "name": "read_file",
        "description": "Read a file",
        "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"path": {"type": "string"}}},
    }}],
    stream=False,  # quiet mode → _force_internal_stream=True → _collect_stream
    max_tokens=200,
)
# Bug: response.choices[0].message.content == "" and tool_calls == None
# Model actually returned a tool_call (finish_reason="tool_calls")
```

**Results** (5 runs each):

| Condition | Content | Tool calls | Result |
|-----------|---------|------------|--------|
| MoA facade **without** tools | 3/3 ✅ | N/A | Normal text response |
| MoA facade **with** tools | 0/3 ❌ | None (hardcoded) | `empty_response_exhausted` crash |
| Direct `curl` with tools | 10/10 ✅ | ✅ `finish_reason=tool_calls` | Model returns tool_call correctly |

## Root Cause

`_collect_stream` (lines 184-224) was written to handle two scenarios:
1. Aggregator outputs text → collect `delta.content`
2. Aggregator outputs reasoning → collect `delta.reasoning_content`

But it misses the third scenario:
3. Aggregator decides to call a tool → `delta.tool_calls` present, `delta.content` empty

The function hardcodes `self_inner.tool_calls = None` (line 207) and `self_inner.finish_reason = "stop"` (line 214), discarding the tool-call response entirely.

## Why `/moa` (interactive TUI) is unaffected

Interactive TUI mode has streaming consumers (`_has_stream_consumers() == True`), so `_use_streaming = True` (conversation_loop.py:1205 condition not met). The MoA facade returns the **raw stream iterator** directly to the streaming consumer, which handles `delta.tool_calls` natively — `_collect_stream` is never called.

Quiet mode (workers, subagents, `-z`) has no streaming consumer, so `_force_internal_stream = True` (moa_loop.py:938), forcing the aggregator's stream through `_collect_stream` — where tool_calls are lost.

## Impact

- **Kanban workers** using MoA crash with `empty_response_exhausted` whenever the aggregator decides to call a tool (which is its intended behavior as acting model)
- **Subagents** (`delegate_task`) using MoA have the same issue
- The crash is intermittent (~33% failure rate in testing) because the aggregator sometimes returns text (works) and sometimes returns tool_calls (crashes)

## Related PRs

- **PR #53848** (merged) — `feat(moa): stream the aggregator response to the user`. Added streaming support for interactive mode, which bypasses `_collect_stream`. This is why `/moa` works.
- **PR #56525** (closed) — `fix(moa): normalize aggregator stream contract for completed responses` by @spiky02plateau. Proposed `_delta_tool_calls` and `_tool_call_arguments_str` helpers at the `MoAChatCompletions.create()` boundary — exactly the tool_calls collection logic that `_collect_stream` is missing. Closed in favor of #56713.
- **PR #56713** (merged) — `fix(streaming): handle completed responses with empty/None choices`. Extended the streaming-consumer guard to cover empty/None choices. This fixes the streaming path but does **not** cover the quiet-mode `_collect_stream` path.

## Suggested Fix

Add `tool_calls` collection to `_collect_stream` (~40 lines):

1. Add `tool_calls_by_index: dict[int, dict]` to merge incremental `delta.tool_calls` chunks by index
2. Accumulate `id`, `function.name`, `function.arguments` across chunks
3. Capture `finish_reason` from stream (don't hardcode `"stop"`)
4. Build `SimpleNamespace` objects for collected tool_calls (to match downstream `tc.id` / `tc.function.name` attribute-access contract)
5. Set `_FakeMessage.tool_calls = collected_tool_calls` (instead of `None`)

I have a working local patch that passes all reproduction tests (0/10 → 10/10 success rate in quiet mode). Happy to open a PR if the approach sounds right.

items.title: Telegram gateway should make busy-time steer/queue/interrupt routing visible

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Summary

Telegram/gateway users have no clear way to tell whether a message sent while an agent is busy was treated as:

- `/steer` into the currently running agent turn,
- queued for the next turn,
- an interrupt/replacement of the running turn, or
- dropped/fallback behavior.

This is especially confusing because explicit `/steer <prompt>` and plain text sent while busy are different mechanisms, but Telegram UX does not make that distinction obvious.

## What happened

While using Hermes through Telegram, I tried to send steering/follow-up instructions while the agent was actively working. From the user side it looked like I had given the agent several mid-run hints, but later inspection showed that the visible Telegram history and the persistent session DB did not make it obvious which of those inputs actually became successful steer injections.

The only reliable confirmation was in logs, e.g. entries like:

```text
Delivered /steer to agent after tool batch
```

Meanwhile, the saved conversation/session history can undercount successful steer events because slash-command handling does not necessarily appear as normal user messages. That made the user-facing audit confusing: a DB/session search suggested fewer steer events than the gateway/agent logs showed.

## Expected behavior

From Telegram, the user should be able to clearly tell what happened to a busy-time message.

For example, when the agent is already running:

- explicit `/steer <text>` should ack with something like:

```text
⏩ Steered into current run — will arrive after the next tool call
```

- if plain text is received while `busy_input_mode: steer`, ack:

```text
⏩ Added as steer to current run
```

- if plain text is received while `busy_input_mode: queue`, ack:

```text
⏳ Queued for next turn
```

- if plain text is received while `busy_input_mode: interrupt`, ack:

```text
⚡ Interrupting current run
```

The exact wording is not important; the important part is that Telegram users should not have to inspect `agent.log` to know whether their input became steer/queue/interrupt.

## Actual behavior

In practice, the Telegram user experience is ambiguous:

1. `/steer <prompt>` can work, but confirmation/audit is mostly log-based.
2. Plain text while busy depends on `display.busy_input_mode`, which may be `interrupt`, `queue`, or `steer`.
3. The current mode is not obvious from Telegram.
4. Saved session history can make successful steer usage look like it did not happen, because slash commands are handled outside normal user-turn persistence.
5. Users may reasonably believe that a normal busy-time text message was a soft steer hint when it was actually handled as queue/interrupt/fallback depending on configuration.

## Why this matters

For Telegram/Discord-style gateway usage, users often continue typing while the agent is working. If they cannot tell whether their message was steered, queued, or interrupted the current work, they lose trust in the system and cannot debug their own workflow.

This is not primarily a request for a localized alias like `/стир`. The bigger problem is observability and UX around busy-time input routing.

## Suggested improvements

1. Add explicit gateway acknowledgements for busy-time routing outcomes:
   - steered
   - queued
   - interrupting
   - rejected/fallback/no active agent

2. Expose busy mode in gateway surfaces, e.g. support `/busy status` or include it in `/status`:

```text
busy_input_mode: interrupt | queue | steer
```

3. Add a user-visible counter or status line for steer events:
   - steer received
   - steer accepted
   - steer delivered
   - steer fallback queued
   - steer rejected

4. Document clearly in the Telegram/gateway docs:
   - `/steer <prompt>` is guaranteed explicit steering.
   - plain text while busy depends on `display.busy_input_mode`.
   - if mode is `interrupt`, plain text is not equivalent to `/steer`.

5. Consider adding structured log/session metadata for slash command outcomes so later audits do not need to scrape free-form logs.

## Related issues noticed before filing

These may overlap but do not fully cover the user-facing observability problem:

- #41572 — slash commands intercepted by busy handler with `busy_input_mode: steer`
- #40683 — `/steer` and slash commands dropped during busy state
- #18362 — `/busy` command not available on Telegram/gateway
- #26024 — configurable busy acknowledgement messages

This issue is specifically about Telegram/gateway UX and auditability: making it clear to a non-terminal user what happened to their busy-time input.

## Environment

- Surface: Telegram gateway
- Repo: `NousResearch/hermes-agent`
- Observed with `/steer`, plain busy-time Telegram input, and gateway/agent logs
- User account filing: `busminer`

items.title: Discord tools can read outside DISCORD_ALLOWED_CHANNELS
items.body:
## Summary
Discord tool calls currently enforce the configured action allowlist at runtime, but channel-scoped target policy is not enforced before REST calls are dispatched. When `DISCORD_ALLOWED_CHANNELS` is set to a specific channel list, a model/tool call can still invoke channel-targeted actions such as `fetch_messages` against another `channel_id`. Guild-wide metadata reads such as `list_channels` also proceed even though a channel-scoped allowlist cannot constrain those results.

## Expected behavior
- Channel-targeted Discord tool actions should refuse channels outside `DISCORD_ALLOWED_CHANNELS`.
- Channels listed in `DISCORD_IGNORED_CHANNELS` should be denied even if a caller provides the channel explicitly.
- Guild-wide metadata reads should require an unrestricted channel policy such as `DISCORD_ALLOWED_CHANNELS=*`, or no channel allowlist at all.

## Proof
I added regression coverage around `tools.discord_tool._discord_request`:

- With `DISCORD_ALLOWED_CHANNELS=11`, `discord_core(action=fetch_messages, channel_id=99)` now returns an error mentioning `DISCORD_ALLOWED_CHANNELS` and `_discord_request` is not called.
- With `DISCORD_ALLOWED_CHANNELS=11`, `discord_admin_handler(action=list_channels, guild_id=111)` now returns an error explaining that the action reads guild-wide metadata and `_discord_request` is not called.
- With `DISCORD_ALLOWED_CHANNELS=*`, the same guild-wide read proceeds normally.

## Duplicate check
Searched existing issues/PRs for:

- `DISCORD_ALLOWED_CHANNELS discord tool list_channels`
- `discord allowed channels server actions guild metadata`
- `discord server_actions allowed_channels`
- `discord tool target allowlist`

I did not find an existing issue covering this runtime target-policy gap.

## Scope
This only covers the Discord tool REST dispatch path in `tools/discord_tool.py`; it does not change inbound Discord adapter behavior, slash command permissions, proxy handling, or action registration.

items.title: Hygiene compression never persists: summary discarded when hygiene agent has no session_db

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
### Bug Description

Context (hygiene) compression is computed but never persisted, so a long-running gateway's transcript grows without bound. `compacted` stays 0 across tens of thousands of messages. In our case the context reached ~112k tokens, which then trips the provider's per-request prompt-size limit (HTTP 402). That also marks the provider unhealthy, which makes the auxiliary model that performs compression unavailable, so compression can never recover on its own.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a self-hosted gateway with default `compression` settings (`in_place: false`).
2. Keep a single session going long enough to cross `compression.threshold`.
3. Observe: the hygiene summary runs, but `compacted` never increments and the stored transcript keeps growing.

### Expected Behavior

When a session crosses the threshold, the computed summary replaces the old messages and the stored transcript shrinks (`compacted` increments).

### Actual Behavior

The summary is computed and then thrown away. In `gateway/run.py` (around the `#21301` guard) the hygiene agent is built without a `session_db`, so `_hyg_in_place` is `False` (`compression_in_place` defaults false) and `_hyg_rotated` is `False` (session_id unchanged). The rewrite is therefore skipped:

```python
if _hyg_rotated or _hyg_in_place:
    self.session_store.rewrite_transcript(session_entry.session_id, _compressed)
else:
    logger.warning(
        "Gateway hygiene compression for session %s did not rotate or "
        "compact in place (no session_db on the hygiene agent) — preserving "
        "the original transcript instead of overwriting it with the summary "
        "(#21301).",
        session_entry.session_id,
    )
```

The only way to make it persist is `compression.in_place: true`, but the surrounding comment flags that path as permanent data loss:

```
# an unconditional rewrite_transcript() would DELETE the original messages
# and replace them with only the compressed summary (permanent data loss, #21301).
```

So with the safe defaults compression is effectively a no-op, and the documented knob to enable it is explicitly unsafe. `compression.threshold` and `target_ratio` have no observable effect.

Production log line:

```
Gateway hygiene compression for session <id> did not rotate or compact in place (no session_db on the hygiene agent) — preserving the original transcript instead of overwriting it with the summary (#21301).
```

Request: give the hygiene agent a `session_db` reference (or a safe rotate-and-replace path) so in-place compaction can persist without the data-loss risk. As it stands, compression cannot take effect with settings that are safe to use.

### Affected Component

Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

### Debug Report

Self-hosted install, analysed at the code level rather than from a captured debug report. Key facts: Hermes 0.15.1, direct-to-OpenRouter provider, `compression.enabled: true`, `threshold: 0.75`, `target_ratio: 0.4`, `in_place: false`; `compacted` = 0 across ~21k messages while a single session reached ~112k tokens.

### Operating System

Debian 13 (Proxmox LXC, unprivileged)

### Python Version

3.13

### Hermes Version

0.15.1

items.title: model_switch tool blocked by _AGENT_LOOP_TOOLS + missing inline handler in sequential executor

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:not-planned
labels.description: Sweeper: closed per standing maintainer policy (design direction)

items.body:
## Description

The `model_switch` tool (`tools/model_switch_tool.py`) allows the agent to autonomously switch its model mid-session. It currently has two issues that prevent it from working outside the agent loop.

## Issue 1: `_AGENT_LOOP_TOOLS` blocks registry dispatch

`model_switch` is in `_AGENT_LOOP_TOOLS` at `model_tools.py:597`, which causes `handle_function_call()` to reject it with "must be handled by the agent loop". Unlike `todo`/`memory`/`session_search`/`delegate_task`, `model_switch` does not need agent state — its handler is self-contained and safely handles the `parent_agent=None` case.

**Fix:** Remove `"model_switch"` from `_AGENT_LOOP_TOOLS`:
```python
_AGENT_LOOP_TOOLS = {"todo", "memory", "session_search", "delegate_task"}
```

## Issue 2: Missing inline handler in sequential executor

The sequential executor (`agent/tool_executor.py` → `execute_tool_calls_sequential`) dispatches unrecognized tools through `handle_function_call()`, which does not pass `parent_agent`. Without `parent_agent`, the handler returns "no agent session".

The concurrent executor already works because it uses `agent._invoke_tool()` → `invoke_tool()` which handles `model_switch` inline with `parent_agent=agent` (see `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py:2214`).

**Fix:** Add an inline handler after the `delegate_task` block in `execute_tool_calls_sequential` (`agent/tool_executor.py`, around line 1327):

```python
        elif function_name == "model_switch":
            def _execute(next_args: dict) -> Any:
                from tools.model_switch_tool import model_switch_tool as _model_switch_tool
                return _model_switch_tool(
                    model=next_args.get("model", ""),
                    provider=next_args.get("provider", ""),
                    parent_agent=agent,
                )
            function_result, function_args = _run_agent_tool_execution_middleware(
                agent,
                function_name=function_name,
                function_args=function_args,
                effective_task_id=effective_task_id,
                tool_call_id=getattr(tool_call, "id", "") or "",
                execute=_execute,
            )
            tool_duration = time.time() - tool_start_time
            if agent._should_emit_quiet_tool_messages():
                agent._vprint(f"  {_get_cute_tool_message_impl(\"model_switch\", function_args, tool_duration, result=function_result)}")
```

Both fixes are small, self-contained, and tested working.

items.body:
## Summary

The shared redactor masks several known API-key prefixes, including `fw_...` Fireworks keys, but it does not currently mask the sibling `fw-...` and `fpk_...` Fireworks token shapes when they appear as bare values in logs, tool output, or gateway-visible text.

If an upstream error, CLI command, or tool output includes one of those bare tokens without a sensitive field name such as `FIREWORKS_API_KEY=...`, the raw credential can remain visible.

## Proof

Using synthetic in-memory token strings only; no real credentials were used.

Before the fix, the current redactor leaks `fw-...` and `fpk_...` while masking `fw_...`:

```text
fw_dash True provider error fw-AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA
fw_under False provider error fw_BBB...BBBB
fpk True provider error fpk_CCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC
```

After adding the missing prefixes, the same redactor masks all three Fireworks token shapes and still leaves short non-key words unchanged:

```text
fw_dash False provider error fw-AAA...AAAA
fw_under False provider error fw_BBB...BBBB
fpk False provider error fpk_CC...CCCC
short fw-tooshort fw_tooshort fpk_tooshort
```

## Expected behavior

Bare Fireworks token families should be treated like other provider API keys by the shared redactor:

- `fw-<long token>`
- `fw_<long token>`
- `fpk_<long token>`

Short ordinary strings such as `fw-tooshort`, `fw_tooshort`, and `fpk_tooshort` should not be redacted.

items.title: MoA: empty user turn in reference advisory view 400s strict providers (Kimi/Moonshot 'role user must not be empty')

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Summary

When MoA (Mixture of Agents) fans out to multiple reference models, a reference running on a **strict provider** (Kimi / Moonshot) fails with a hard HTTP 400 while a reference on a **lenient provider** (DeepSeek) succeeds — for the *identical* rendered advisory view. The user-facing symptom looks like "Kimi doesn't support MoA", but the real cause is an **empty user turn leaking into the advisory transcript** that `_reference_messages()` builds.

Observed error (reference slot `kimi-coding-cn:kimi-k2.6`):

```
[failed: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': "Invalid request: the message
at position 1 with role 'user' must not be empty", 'type': 'invalid_request_error'}}]
```

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: `main` (verified against `agent/moa_loop.py`)
- OS: macOS
- MoA preset: two reference models — `deepseek:deepseek-v4-pro` (passes) and `kimi-coding-cn:kimi-k2.6` (400s), aggregator on OpenRouter Claude
- Trigger: a multi-turn tool-calling conversation (not a fresh single-shot prompt)

## Root Cause

`agent/moa_loop.py` → `_reference_messages()` builds the advisory view handed to every reference model. Its `user` branch appends **unconditionally**, even when the extracted text is empty:

```python
text = content if isinstance(content, str) else ""   # non-string/multimodal -> ""
...
if role == "user":
    if text.strip():
        last_user_content = text
    rendered.append({"role": "user", "content": text})   # <-- appends even when text == ""
```

Two ways an empty user turn arises in a real transcript:

1. A user-role message with `content == ""` in history.
2. A user message whose `content` is a **non-string / multimodal payload** (a list of content blocks). The `text = content if isinstance(content, str) else ""` line flattens it to `""`, then the empty string is appended verbatim.

The `assistant` branch already **drops** turns that carry no parts (empty text + no tool_calls). The `user` branch does not have the equivalent guard, so an empty user message survives into the request payload.

Strict providers (Kimi/Moonshot) reject an empty-content user message with `400 ... role 'user' must not be empty`. Lenient providers (DeepSeek, and OpenAI/Anthropic official) accept it. Within one fan-out over the same view, that means **one reference 400s and another passes** — which reads as a provider-specific MoA incompatibility but is actually a message-construction bug.

This is a sibling of the strict-backend normalization issues already tracked (#31583 for empty *assistant* content, #29327 for strict-backend history normalization), but on a distinct code path: the MoA **advisory view**, `user` role, `_reference_messages()`.

## Reproduction

Minimal, no network needed:

```python
from agent.moa_loop import _reference_messages

msgs = [
    {"role": "system", "content": "hermes boilerplate"},
    {"role": "user", "content": "how do I configure moa"},
    {"role": "assistant", "content": "", "tool_calls": [
        {"function": {"name": "read_file", "arguments": '{"path":"config.yaml"}'}}]},
    {"role": "tool", "content": "moa: enabled true"},
    {"role": "user", "content": ""},                                   # empty user turn
    {"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "multimodal"}]},  # non-string -> ""
]

view = _reference_messages(msgs)
empties = [m for m in view if m["role"] == "user" and not str(m["content"]).strip()]
print("empty user messages in view:", len(empties))   # BEFORE fix: >= 1  ->  Kimi 400s
```

Any reference slot pointed at Kimi/Moonshot then 400s on this view; a DeepSeek slot succeeds.

## Fix

Skip empty user turns in `_reference_messages()`, mirroring the existing empty-assistant-turn handling. The end-on-user invariant is preserved (the synthetic advisory-request user turn is still appended when the view would otherwise end on an assistant turn).

PR: (see linked pull request below) — includes a regression test asserting the advisory view contains no empty user turn and still ends on a user turn.

items.body:
## Summary

Hermes suppresses completed gateway replies only when the whole response is exactly a silence marker such as `NO_REPLY`, `NO REPLY`, `SILENT`, or `[SILENT]`.

When the model adds stray edge punctuation around the marker, the filter misses it and the control text can be delivered visibly to chat surfaces. Examples that currently miss:

- `.NO_REPLY`
- `*NO_REPLY*`
- ` .NO_REPLY `
- `*[SILENT]*`

This is confusing for users because these are still token-only silence replies; the punctuation is just model formatting noise.

## Proof

Current behavior before the fix, using the real `gateway.response_filters.is_intentional_silence_response` helper:

```text
'NO_REPLY' True
'.NO_REPLY' False
'*NO_REPLY*' False
' .NO_REPLY ' False
'😄 NO_REPLY' False
'the sentinel is NO_REPLY, fyi' False
'[SILENT]' True
'*[SILENT]*' False
```

After the fix, punctuation-wrapped token-only markers suppress correctly, while emoji/prose and malformed `[SILENT` stay visible:

```text
'NO_REPLY' True
'.NO_REPLY' True
'*NO_REPLY*' True
' .NO_REPLY ' True
'😄 NO_REPLY' False
'the sentinel is NO_REPLY, fyi' False
'[SILENT]' True
'*[SILENT]*' True
'[SILENT' False
```

## Expected behavior

The gateway should try the exact silence-marker match first, then tolerate stray Unicode punctuation at the response edges. It should not suppress substantive prose that merely mentions the marker, and it should not strip emoji into a false positive.

items.title: Gateway proxy SSE parser can buffer an unbounded boundary-less line

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
﻿## Summary

Gateway proxy mode parses successful `/v1/chat/completions` SSE streams by appending decoded chunks into a local `buffer` and splitting only when a newline arrives:

```python
buffer += text
while "\n" in buffer:
    line, buffer = buffer.split("\n", 1)
```

If the remote proxy sends a long malformed or boundary-less SSE line, the residual `buffer` has no cap. A stalled or buggy upstream can therefore grow gateway memory until the process is killed or the OS/network eventually closes the socket.

## Proof

Source-level proof on current `main`:

- `gateway/run.py::_run_agent_via_proxy` sets `buffer = ""` for the successful SSE path.
- Each chunk from `resp.content.iter_any()` is appended to `buffer` before parsing.
- Completed lines are removed, but a stream with no newline leaves all bytes in `buffer`.
- There is no length check on that residual successful-stream buffer.

The focused regression added with the fix sets a tiny cap and streams `b"data: "` followed by a boundary-less chunk. Before this fix, that path keeps accumulating because no line boundary is present. After this fix, the gateway returns a proxy connection error instead of continuing to buffer.

## Duplicate check

I checked the obvious existing proxy/SSE work before filing:

- #9834 covers `[DONE]` loop exit, TCP connect timeout, and malformed JSON chunk handling in the same proxy SSE loop.
- #55016 covers non-200 proxy error response body caps.

Neither covers the successful SSE path's residual line/event buffer when no newline boundary arrives.

## Expected behavior

The successful proxy SSE parser should keep normal completed SSE lines unchanged, but abort when the unprocessed residual buffer exceeds a bounded size without seeing a line boundary.

items.title: [Bug]: Slack block extraction debug log includes message text preview
items.body:
## Bug Description

Slack inbound message handling logs the text extracted from rich-text Block Kit payloads at debug level.

When a Slack message includes quoted or forwarded rich-text content, `_handle_slack_message()` merges that block text into the agent-visible message. The merge is correct, but the debug log currently includes a preview of the extracted text. With debug logging enabled, private message content can be copied into gateway logs even though the log line only needs to report that block text was appended.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the Slack gateway with debug logging enabled.
2. Send a Slack message whose `blocks` contain rich-text quote content not already present in the plain `text` field.
3. Observe the gateway debug log from `plugins.platforms.slack.adapter`.

## Expected Behavior

The log should include metadata only, such as that additional block text was extracted and its length.

## Actual Behavior

The debug log includes a message-content preview via the extracted rich-text block content.

## Affected Component

- Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)
- Slack

## Source-level Proof

`plugins/platforms/slack/adapter.py::_handle_slack_message` logs `stripped_blocks[:300]` when `_extract_text_from_slack_blocks()` returns text not already present in the plain message body. That value comes from user-supplied Slack rich-text blocks.

A focused regression test can construct a Slack event with a sensitive quoted rich-text block and assert that the handler still logs the extraction event without logging the quoted content.

## Proposed Fix

Keep the debug log, but replace the message preview with metadata such as the extracted character count.

items.body:
### Bug Description
With `terminal.backend: docker` (OrbStack as Docker provider on macOS), the Desktop app's embedded terminal pane hangs indefinitely on `Connecting to hermes-63681334.orb.local...`. The agent's own terminal tool works perfectly through the same container (docker exec via socket) — only the visual pane fails.

### Environment
- Hermes Desktop 0.17.0 (source build, main @ 5445e42), macOS (Apple Silicon)
- Docker provider: **OrbStack** (docker CLI at `~/.orbstack/bin/docker`, PATH set in `~/.zshrc`)
- `terminal.backend: docker`, `container_persistent: true`, image `nikolaik/python-nodejs:python3.11-nodejs20`

### Ruled out
- DNS: `*.orb.local` resolves; a test HTTP server in the container at `http://<container>.orb.local:8080` loads fine in a browser. NextDNS fully disabled → no change.
- Container health: running; agent terminal/file tools work through it the entire time.
- No related traceback in `desktop.log` — suggesting the failure is in the Electron main process PTY spawn, not the Python backend.

### Suspected root cause
#44298 added backend-following pane support via `docker exec -it <container> bash` spawned by node-pty in the Electron main process. GUI-launched Electron doesn't inherit shell PATH from `~/.zshrc`, so OrbStack's `docker` binary (`~/.orbstack/bin/docker`, not `/usr/local/bin`) is likely not found → spawn fails → UI stuck on "Connecting…" with no error surfaced.

### Expected Behavior
Pane attaches to the container shell, or fails fast with a visible error (e.g. "docker CLI not found").

### Suggested fix
Resolve the docker binary the same way the Python backend's `find_docker()` does (check `~/.orbstack/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`), and surface spawn errors in the pane instead of hanging.

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Summary
`${VAR}` environment references are expanded in the `providers.*` block but **not** in the `auxiliary.*` block, so per-task auxiliary credentials configured as env refs are passed to the provider client literally.

## Repro (on `main`)
1. Set an env-ref key on an auxiliary task, e.g.:
   ```yaml
   auxiliary:
     vision:
       provider: custom
       model: meta/llama-3.2-11b-vision-instruct
       base_url: https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1
       api_key: ${NVIDIA_API_KEY}
   ```
2. `NVIDIA_API_KEY` is set in `.env`.
3. Inspect the resolved value:
   ```python
   from hermes_cli.config import load_config
   print(load_config()["auxiliary"]["vision"]["api_key"])
   # -> "${NVIDIA_API_KEY}"  (literal, NOT expanded)
   ```
4. The literal string is sent as the API key → auth failure / silent misroute to a fallback provider.

By contrast, `providers.mistral.api_key: ${MISTRAL_API_KEY}` **does** expand — so the behavior is inconsistent between the two config regions.

## Expected
The recursive `${VAR}` expansion pass (hermes_cli/config.py, ~line 6045) should also cover the `auxiliary.*` subtree so `auxiliary.<task>.api_key` / `base_url` honor env refs like `providers.*` do.

## Impact
Users configuring an auxiliary vision/compression/etc. endpoint with an env-ref key get a broken endpoint with no obvious error; the request silently falls through to another provider. Workaround is to inline the literal secret in `config.yaml`, which defeats the `.env`-for-secrets convention.

## Environment
macOS, Hermes on `main`. Found while wiring `auxiliary.vision` to an NVIDIA NIM VLM.

items.title: _resolve_task_provider_model ignores auxiliary.<task>.base_url when provider passed explicitly

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Summary
In `agent/auxiliary_client.py`, `_resolve_task_provider_model` returns early when an explicit `provider` argument is supplied, which skips the config block that honors `auxiliary.<task>.base_url` / `api_key`. A configured custom endpoint is then bypassed in favor of the main runtime.

## Location
`agent/auxiliary_client.py`, `_resolve_task_provider_model`, ~line 5505:

```python
if base_url and _preserve_provider_with_base_url(provider):
    return provider, resolved_model, base_url, api_key, resolved_api_mode
if base_url:
    return "custom", resolved_model, base_url, api_key, resolved_api_mode
if provider:                       # <-- fires for an explicit provider arg
    return provider, resolved_model, base_url, api_key, resolved_api_mode
    #    base_url here is the (None) explicit arg; cfg_base_url is ignored

if task:
    # config block that DOES honor cfg_base_url / cfg_api_key ...
    if cfg_base_url and cfg_api_key:
        return "custom", resolved_model, cfg_base_url, cfg_api_key, resolved_api_mode
    ...
```

When a caller passes `provider` explicitly but no `base_url`, the `if provider:` branch returns before the `if task:` block, so `auxiliary.<task>.base_url`/`api_key` from config are never consulted.

## Repro
```python
from agent.auxiliary_client import resolve_vision_provider_client
# auxiliary.vision configured as a custom NIM endpoint in config.yaml
p, c, m = resolve_vision_provider_client(provider="custom", model="meta/llama-3.2-11b-vision-instruct")
print(getattr(c, "base_url", None))
# -> https://api.deepseek.com/v1/   (main runtime, NOT the configured aux base_url)
```
Calling it with **no** explicit provider (the real vision-task path) works correctly and routes to the configured endpoint — so this is latent for the built-in vision path but bites any caller that passes `provider` explicitly.

## Expected
When `provider` is explicit but `base_url` is not, still consult `cfg_base_url` / `cfg_api_key` for the task before returning, rather than dropping into `_resolve_custom_runtime`/main-runtime resolution.

## Environment
macOS, Hermes on `main`.

items.body:
## Summary

A CLI-created session did not appear in hermes-webui's session list for continuation while the CLI turn was still in progress / before final assistant output, even though the session had already produced many tool calls and was persisted. A session should be visible and resumable from hermes-webui as soon as it exists in `state.db` (at least after the first user turn is persisted), not only after a final assistant message or terminal shutdown.

Observed local session:

- session id: `20260704_170619_2a8e6e`
- source: `cli`
- started: `2026-07-04T17:07:35.556677`
- `ended_at`: `NULL` (CLI terminal was accidentally closed later)
- row exists in `C:\Apps\hermes\state.db`
- messages were present while the run was active; by later inspection the session had 77+ messages / 34 API calls
- source cache also had an entry under `C:\Apps\hermes\webui\sessions\_index.json`

## Why this looks like a bug

The source trace shows the CLI side does persist sessions to the same session DB that the WebUI session list API reads from:

1. CLI/agent lazy-creates the DB row in `run_agent.py`:

```py
# run_agent.py:600-617
def _ensure_db_session(self) -> None:
    """Create session DB row on first use. Disables _session_db on failure."""
    if getattr(self, "_persist_disabled", False):
        return
    if self._session_db_created or not self._session_db:
        return
    source = _session_source_for_agent(self.platform)
    try:
        self._session_db.create_session(
            session_id=self.session_id,
            source=source,
            model=self.model,
            model_config=self._session_init_model_config,
            system_prompt=self._cached_system_prompt,
            user_id=None,
            parent_session_id=self._parent_session_id,
            cwd=_launch_cwd_for_session(source),
        )
```

2. Turn setup explicitly creates the DB row after the system prompt is available and persists the inbound user turn for crash resilience:

```py
# agent/turn_context.py:322-329
# Create the DB session row now that _cached_system_prompt is populated, so
# the persisted snapshot is written non-NULL on the first turn (Issue
# #45499). Idempotent: _ensure_db_session() no-ops once the row exists.
agent._ensure_db_session()

# Crash-resilience: persist the inbound user turn as soon as the session row exists.
try:
    agent._persist_session(messages, conversation_history)
```

3. The WebUI session API reads from `SessionDB.list_sessions_rich(...)` and does not filter out `source=cli` by default:

```py
# hermes_cli/web_server.py:3509-3567
@app.get("/api/sessions")
async def get_sessions(
    limit: int = 20,
    offset: int = 0,
    min_messages: int = 0,
    archived: str = "exclude",
    order: str = "created",
    source: str = None,
    exclude_sources: str = None,
    cwd_prefix: str = None,
    profile: Optional[str] = None,
):
    ...
    sessions = db.list_sessions_rich(
        source=source or None,
        exclude_sources=exclude_list or None,
        cwd_prefix=(cwd_prefix or None),
        limit=limit,
        offset=offset,
        min_message_count=min_message_count,
        include_archived=include_archived,
        archived_only=archived_only,
        order_by_last_active=order == "recent",
    )
```

4. The chat session picker uses that API with `order=recent`:

```ts
// web/src/components/ChatSessionList.tsx:83-100
const load = useCallback(() => {
  const myReq = ++reqRef.current;
  setLoading(true);
  setError(null);
  api
    .getSessions(SESSION_LIMIT, 0, scopeKey, "recent")
    .then((res) => {
      if (reqRef.current !== myReq) return;
      setSessions(res.sessions);
    })
```

```ts
// web/src/lib/api.ts:352-363
getSessions: (
  limit = 20,
  offset = 0,
  profile = getManagementProfile(),
  order: "created" | "recent" = "created",
) =>
  fetchJSON<PaginatedSessions>(
    appendProfileParam(
      `/api/sessions?limit=${limit}&offset=${offset}&order=${order}`,
      profile,
    ),
  ),
```

So, by code path, a CLI session that is in `state.db` with `source='cli'`, non-archived, non-child, and recent activity should be returned to the picker. In this case it was not visible in hermes-webui when the user tried to resume it.

## Local evidence

SQLite state after the incident:

```text
State DB row:
id 20260704_170619_2a8e6e
source cli
started_at 1783199255.556677 2026-07-04T17:07:35.556677
ended_at None
end_reason None

cwd C:\Users\Rod
api_call_count 34

```

Recent ordering emulation against `state.db` showed the CLI session should be on the first page:

```text
Top recent list (state.db emulation):
0 20260704_174401_bec6a5 cli 137 2026-07-04T17:59:19.455148 None
1 20260704_170619_2a8e6e cli 77 2026-07-04T17:58:45.527475 Last Week Gate Certification
2 c2f61bf27695 api_server 8 2026-07-03T23:23:51.399449 None

4 03a1f74cc4e0 api_server 2 2026-07-03T22:40:29.599630 None
```

The WebUI session cache/index also contained the same session, though with stale-ish metadata compared with `state.db`:

```text
WebUI cache index:

title grep nesquena-hermes Gate certification
message_count 38
created_at 1783199255.556677
updated_at 1783202327.0899916
last_message_at 1783202327.0087876
```

Agent log excerpts show the session was active and doing tool/API work well before it ended:

```text
2026-07-04 17:46:31,271 INFO [20260704_170619_2a8e6e] agent.tool_executor: tool terminal completed (0.26s, 152 chars)
2026-07-04 17:46:39,807 INFO [20260704_170619_2a8e6e] agent.conversation_loop: API call #8: model=gpt-5.5 provider=openai-api in=24484 out=198 total=24682 latency=8.5s cache=24064/24484 (98%)
```

## Expected behavior

If a session starts in CLI and the DB row/user turn has been persisted, hermes-webui should show it in the resume/continue list immediately, even while the CLI agent is still running tools or waiting for/finalizing an assistant answer.

`resolve_anthropic_token()` in `agent/anthropic_adapter.py` checks Claude Code's


This is adjacent to #31668 / #40014 / #47260 / #53212, but distinct: those are
about the OAuth/subscription request itself being misclassified as overage.
This report is about the **credential resolver picking OAuth over an explicit
API key even when the API key is present and correctly configured** — so the
user never gets a chance to actually use the key they set up.

## Root cause

`resolve_anthropic_token()` (agent/anthropic_adapter.py) resolves credentials
in this order:

1. `ANTHROPIC_TOKEN` env
2. `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` env
3. Claude Code credential file (`~/.claude/.credentials.json`) — **unconditional auto-discovery, no gate**
4. Hermes credential_pool OAuth entry
5. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` env — **explicit key, checked last**

Steps 1–2 are explicit env vars, so it's reasonable for them to win. But step 3
is pure auto-discovery with no check for whether the user already configured
an explicit key — so it always wins over step 5 whenever Claude Code is
logged in, regardless of user intent.

This also means the "Anthropic API key" path in `hermes model`
(`hermes_cli/model_setup_flows.py:_model_flow_anthropic`, `choice == "2"`)
doesn't actually work as advertised for anyone with Claude Code installed and
logged in: `save_anthropic_api_key()` writes `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` into
`~/.hermes/.env` and clears `ANTHROPIC_TOKEN`, but never touches the Claude
Code credential-file auto-discovery, so the saved key is silently shadowed at
call time.

Notably, this exact class of bug was already fixed for the **credential_pool**
path via `is_provider_explicitly_configured()` (referenced in
`hermes_cli/model_switch.py` as "gates anthropic behind
`is_provider_explicitly_configured()` to prevent auxiliary tasks from silently
consuming Claude Code tokens (PR #4210)") — but that guard was never applied
to the direct Claude-Code-credential-file check inside
`resolve_anthropic_token()` itself.

## Repro

1. Log into Claude Code CLI (`claude login`) on a machine with a Pro/Max plan.
2. In Hermes, run `hermes model` → Anthropic → choose "2. Anthropic API key" → paste a valid `sk-ant-api03-...` key.
3. `hermes status` correctly shows `Anthropic ✓ sk-a...XXXX`.
4. Send any message to the agent with Anthropic/Claude selected as provider.
5. Observe the request actually goes out with the Claude Code OAuth token (`sk-ant-oat01-...`), not the configured API key, and (if extra-usage is exhausted) fails with the 400 shown above.

Verified directly:
```python
from hermes_cli.env_loader import load_hermes_dotenv
load_hermes_dotenv(hermes_home=Path.home() / ".hermes", project_env=None)
from agent.anthropic_adapter import resolve_anthropic_token
resolve_anthropic_token()  # -> 'sk-ant-oat01-...' even with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set in ~/.hermes/.env
```

## Proposed fix

Move the explicit `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` check ahead of the Claude Code
credential-file / credential-pool auto-discovery steps, so an explicitly
configured key always wins over auto-detected OAuth. Patch (applied locally,
tested — after the change `resolve_anthropic_token()` returns the configured
`sk-ant-api03-...` key instead of the auto-discovered `sk-ant-oat01-...`
token):

```diff
--- a/agent/anthropic_adapter.py
+++ b/agent/anthropic_adapter.py
@@ -1277,10 +1277,13 @@ def resolve_anthropic_token() -> Optional[str]:
     Priority:
       1. ANTHROPIC_TOKEN env var (OAuth/setup token saved by Hermes)
       2. CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN env var
-      3. Claude Code credentials (~/.claude.json or ~/.claude/.credentials.json)
+      3. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY env var (explicit API key) — checked ahead of the
+         auto-discovered Claude Code credential file/pool below so a
+         deliberately configured key is never silently shadowed by a logged-in
+         Claude Code session.
+      4. Claude Code credentials (~/.claude.json or ~/.claude/.credentials.json)
          — with automatic refresh if expired and a refresh token is available
-      4. Anthropic credential_pool OAuth entry (~/.hermes/auth.json)
-      5. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY env var (regular API key, or legacy fallback)
+      5. Anthropic credential_pool OAuth entry (~/.hermes/auth.json)
 
     Returns the token string or None.
     """
@@ -1302,22 +1305,21 @@ def resolve_anthropic_token() -> Optional[str]:
             return preferred
         return cc_token
 
-    # 3. Claude Code credential file
+    # 3. Regular API key — explicit configuration wins over auto-discovery.
+    api_key = os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", "").strip()
+    if api_key:
+        return api_key
+
+    # 4. Claude Code credential file
     resolved_claude_token = _resolve_claude_code_token_from_credentials(creds)
     if resolved_claude_token:
         return resolved_claude_token
 
-    # 4. Hermes credential_pool OAuth entry.
+    # 5. Hermes credential_pool OAuth entry.
     resolved_pool_token = _resolve_anthropic_pool_token()
     if resolved_pool_token:
         return resolved_pool_token
 
-    # 5. Regular API key, or a legacy OAuth token saved in ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
-    # This remains as a compatibility fallback for pre-migration Hermes configs.
-    api_key = os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", "").strip()
-    if api_key:
-        return api_key
-
     return None
```

## Environment

- Hermes Agent (venv-installed, `hermes-agent` repo, current `main` as of 2026-07-04)
- Linux, Python 3.11.15
- Provider: Anthropic, Model: claude-sonnet-5
