items.title: Cache-stack: Six features for prompt-cache optimisation
items.body:
## Problem Statement

Hermes Agent pays for 8-15K uncached input tokens on every API turn — 127 skill descriptions, user profile, memory blocks, 40+ full JSON tool schemas, environment hints, and project context files are re-serialised into the system prompt each session. When context compression fires, the system prompt is rebuilt from scratch, invalidating the prefix cache. Tool results from a 12KB file read haunt every future turn indefinitely. All auxiliary calls (compression, vision, title generation) use the same expensive model as the main conversation.

In contrast, agent runtimes like Reasonix achieve 99.82% prefix-cache hit rates on DeepSeek by keeping a byte-stable immutable prefix, an append-only conversation log, per-turn volatile scratch that never enters the cached prefix, tool-result auto-compaction, flash-first model routing, and leaner system prompts. The resulting cost difference is ~80-91% per day of active use.

## Solution

Implement six cache-optimising features in Hermes Agent, each gated behind a config flag and landed as an independent PR:

1. **Tool-result auto-compaction** — cap old tool results at a configurable token limit after each turn. The model sees the full result during the active turn; subsequent turns see a head+tail compacted version with a truncation marker.

2. **Volatile scratch separation** — split the system prompt into a byte-stable cached prefix (identity, tool guidance, context files) and a per-turn volatile block (memory, user profile, timestamp). The prefix stays warm across turns; only the volatile tail changes.

3. **Leaner skill index** — compact non-coding skill categories to names-only by default, reducing the skills section of the system prompt by ~30% without hiding any skill from `skill_view`/`skills_list`.

4. **Flash-first model routing** — default to a cheaper/faster model, auto-escalate to a premium model on `/pro`, 3+ tool-call repair events, or `<<<NEEDS_PRO>>>` marker. All auxiliary calls hard-code the cheap tier.

5. **Tool schema byte-stability and compaction** — verify and enforce byte-identical tool schema serialisation across calls (prevents cache-breaking dict-ordering drift), then optionally strip non-essential fields from schemas.

6. **Cache-safe compression** — when context compression fires, splice a summary assistant message into the history instead of rebuilding the system prompt from scratch. The cached prefix survives compression.

All features respect Hermes's "prompt caching is sacred" invariant — no mid-conversation prefix mutation, strict role alternation, byte-stable across turns.

## User Stories

1. As a Hermes user on DeepSeek, I want tool results compacted after each turn so that reading a large file doesn't permanently bloat my context and cost tokens on every future API call.

2. As a Hermes user with a long-running session, I want the system prompt prefix to stay byte-stable across turns so that DeepSeek's prefix cache stays warm and I pay cached rates (~$0.028/M) instead of uncached rates (~$0.139/M) for input tokens.

3. As a Hermes user who writes to memory during a session, I want my memory updates to be reflected without breaking the prompt cache so I get both fresh context AND cache savings.

4. As a cost-conscious Hermes user, I want most turns to default to a cheaper model (e.g., v4-flash) and only escalate to an expensive model (e.g., v4-pro) when the task genuinely needs stronger reasoning.

5. As a Hermes user who never uses creative/smart-home/media skills, I want those skill descriptions excluded from my system prompt so I don't pay tokens for capability I never invoke.

6. As a Hermes user on any provider, I want tool schemas to be as compact as possible so every API call ships fewer input tokens.

7. As a Hermes user on a long session, I want context compression to NOT break my prompt cache so the cost savings from features 1-6 aren't lost the moment compression fires.

8. As a Hermes user who wants to opt out, I want every cache feature gated behind a config flag so I can disable anything that doesn't work for my provider or workflow.

9. As a developer contributing to Hermes, I want tool schemas to be byte-stable across calls so I can verify that serialisation drift isn't silently breaking the cache.

10. As a gateway user running Hermes on Telegram/Discord, I want these cache features to work identically to the CLI so my messaging sessions get the same cost savings.

11. As a Hermes user who occasionally needs strong reasoning, I want to type `/pro` to escalate for one turn and have it auto-disarm afterwards so I don't accidentally stay on the expensive tier.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Six independent features, one PR each.** Land order: tool compaction → volatile scratch → leaner skills → flash-first routing → schema compaction → cache-safe compression. Features 3 and 4 explicitly require Feature 2 to land first.

- **Config gating.** All risky features default off (`model.routing.enabled: false`, `compression.append_only: false`, `agent.compact_tool_schemas: false`). Tool compaction defaults on (`tool_result_cap_tokens: 3000`) because it's low-risk. Leaner skills default on for non-coding categories.

- **Consolidated routing config.** An existing `smart_model_routing` key (set by blank-slate setup) is migrated to `model.routing.enabled`. The old key is dropped from setup.

- **Append-only compression builds on existing `in_place`.** Feature 4 is additive — when both `compression.in_place: true` (default) and `compression.append_only: true` (new), compression keeps the same session_id AND splices a summary without rebuilding the prompt.

- **Role alternation proven for summary injection.** The summary message replaces the oldest complete turns, positioned as `[system] → [assistant_summary] → [user_K]` — no two same-role messages adjacent.

- **Tool schemas verified byte-stable before compacting.** A `json.dumps(sort_keys=True)` comparison test proves no serialisation drift exists before Feature 6 strips fields.

- **Volatile block at END of system message.** DeepSeek's prefix cache keys on the shared byte prefix. Putting volatile content at the tail means the prefix stays cached even when the tail changes per turn.

- **Auxiliary resolution order.** When routing is enabled: explicit `auxiliary.<task>.provider` wins → `model.routing.default` (cheap tier) → never escalation tier. Nine auxiliary tasks affected.

## Testing Decisions

- **Seams tested in isolation.** Each feature exposes one pure function or module boundary — no private internals tested. `compact_tool_results()`, `build_volatile_block()`, `resolve_model_for_turn()` are all testable at the public interface.

- **Behaviour contracts, not snapshots.** Tests assert invariants (prefix byte-stable across turns, no two same-role messages after compression, tool results compacted at the right boundary). No change-detector tests that freeze byte sizes or token counts.

- **E2E validation.** Real `hermes chat` session against DeepSeek with before/after cache-hit rate comparison via DeepSeek dashboard.

- **Prior art.** Follows the pattern of existing `tests/agent/test_context_compressor_*.py` for compression tests, `tests/agent/test_prompt_builder.py` for prompt assembly tests. New test files for compaction, routing, and schema compaction.

- **Full suite gate.** `scripts/run_tests.sh` must pass with all new tests before each PR is ready.

## Out of Scope

- Measurement infrastructure (cost-per-session tracking, automated cache-hit rate monitoring)
- Automated E2E cache-hit verification harness
- Provider-specific cache strategy documentation (Anthropic `cache_control`, Google Gemini context caching API)
- Tool removal or consolidation — schema compaction only strips non-essential fields, never removes tools
- Dynamic tool registration at runtime (would break the immutable prefix)
- Per-provider pricing integration (the features work for all providers; cost savings vary by provider's caching model)

## Further Notes

- Plan document: `.hermes/plans/20260705_cache-stack.md` (with completeness review and Advisor findings merged)
- Reference skill: `reasonix-cache-architecture` (captures the architectural patterns from Reasonix's 99.82% cache-hit design)
- Advisor run: `adv_20260704_230212_3725ac4d` — 17 findings, all resolved
- Features 1+5+6 alone: ~30-50% input token reduction before any cache effects
- Features 2+4 combined: prefix cache stays warm across ~100% of turns vs estimated <20% today
- Feature 3: ~10x cost reduction on non-escalated turns (flash vs pro pricing)
- Overall target: 80-91% cost savings on DeepSeek sessions

After upgrading to v0.18.0, all Discord messages are silently dropped. No error is logged. The gateway shows "✓ discord connected" and on_message fires, but messages never reach _handle_message.

Root cause: _is_allowed_user() was changed so that when both _allowed_user_ids and _allowed_role_ids are empty, it now calls _discord_channel_ids_allowed() and returns its result. Since DISCORD_ALLOWED_CHANNELS is not set, that returns False — blocking everyone.

Previous behavior: Empty allowlists = everyone allowed (backwards compatible).

Workaround: Set DISCORD_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true in ~/.hermes/.env. But this should not be required — the old default (allow all when no allowlists configured) should be restored.

Affected: Any user without DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS, DISCORD_ALLOWED_ROLES, or DISCORD_ALLOWED_CHANNELS configured. This is likely the default state for most users.

Version: v0.18.0 (2026.7.1)

items.title: Native Windows: main.py omits hermes_home in load_hermes_dotenv → .env never loaded
items.body:
## Summary

On native Windows, a fresh install fails with **`No inference provider configured`** even when `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\.env` contains a valid `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (or any provider key). The `.env` file is never loaded because the installed `hermes` entrypoint resolves the Hermes home to the POSIX default `~/.hermes` instead of the Windows-native `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes`.

## Root cause

The console-script entrypoint is `hermes_cli.main:main`. At import time `hermes_cli/main.py` loads the dotenv:

```python
# hermes_cli/main.py:519
load_hermes_dotenv(project_env=PROJECT_ROOT / ".env")
```

`hermes_home` is **not** passed. In `env_loader.load_hermes_dotenv`:

```python
home_path = Path(hermes_home or os.getenv("HERMES_HOME", Path.home() / ".hermes"))
```

With `hermes_home=None` and `HERMES_HOME` unset (the default), `home_path` becomes `Path.home() / ".hermes"` = `C:\Users\<user>\.hermes` — which does not exist on Windows. The real home (per `hermes_constants.get_hermes_home()` / `_get_platform_default_hermes_home()`) is `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes`. So the user's `.env` is silently skipped.

`hermes config show` masks the bug: it *displays* the correct path via `get_env_path()` (which uses `get_hermes_home()`), so the "Secrets" line reads `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\.env`, but the actual dotenv load used the wrong directory. Result: every key shows `(not set)`.

Notably `main.py` already imports the correct helper two lines above but doesn't use it:

```python
# main.py:516
from hermes_cli.config import get_hermes_home
```

And the other entrypoint gets it right — `cli.py:182`:

```python
load_hermes_dotenv(hermes_home=_hermes_home, project_env=_project_env)
```

## Reproduce

1. Native Windows (no WSL), `HERMES_HOME` unset.
2. Install, then write a key to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\.env`:
   `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...`
3. `hermes config show` → **Anthropic (not set)**; `hermes` → **No inference provider configured** (error text even points at `~/.hermes/.env`).

Workaround: set `HERMES_HOME=%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes` as a user env var — but that shouldn't be required, since `get_hermes_home()` already knows the correct default.

## Fix

Pass the resolved home, matching `cli.py`:

```python
load_hermes_dotenv(hermes_home=get_hermes_home(), project_env=PROJECT_ROOT / ".env")
```

PR attached.

_Environment: Windows 11, Hermes 0.18.0, local editable (`uv pip install -e .`), Python 3.13._

## Environment
- hermes-agent 0.18.0, checkout at 7203898ce
- Windows 11 Home (10.0.26200), Python 3.11.15
- Standalone web dashboard started with `hermes dashboard` (default port 9119), used from Chrome

## Symptom
After running `hermes update`, the web dashboard's chat never reconnects. The update output shows the asymmetry:

```
→ Stopping Windows gateway process(es) before updating Hermes...
  ✓ Paused gateway profile(s): default
...
✓ Update complete!
  ✓ Restarting Windows gateway profile(s): default
```

The pre-update stop takes down the dashboard server along with the gateway, but the post-update resume only restarts the gateway profile. Nothing listens on 9119 afterward, so any open dashboard tab shows a dead chat connection with no hint that the server is gone. The user-visible failure is "chat not connecting" — it looks like a gateway or network problem, not a missing process.

## Related: `hermes dashboard --status` reports false positives
While diagnosing, `hermes dashboard --status` claimed dashboards were running when none was listening:

```
3 hermes dashboard process(es) running:
    PID 16488
    PID 25324
    PID 31924
```

- 16488 / 25324 were the **desktop app's** internal `serve --port 0` backend (IPC-gated, not a usable dashboard)
- 31924 no longer existed at all

So the natural post-update health check also lies, which makes the missing-dashboard state harder to spot.

## Suggested fix
Track the dashboard server the same way gateway profiles are tracked, and either restart it in the post-update resume step or print an explicit "dashboard was stopped — run `hermes dashboard` to restore the web UI" notice. Separately, `--status` should verify the recorded PIDs are alive and actually bound to a listening port before reporting them as running.

`vision_analyze` fails to route through the configured `auxiliary.vision` provider when the primary model is text-only (DeepSeek V4 Pro). All vision requests are sent to the primary model instead of the auxiliary fallback, causing every call to fail with DeepSeeks "unknown variant image_url, expected text" error.

## To Reproduce

1. Set primary model to DeepSeek (any variant):
   ```
   hermes config set model.default deepseek-v4-pro
   hermes config set model.provider deepseek
   ```
2. Configure auxiliary vision to use OpenRouter + Gemini Flash:
   ```
   hermes config set auxiliary.vision.provider openrouter
   hermes config set auxiliary.vision.model google/gemini-2.5-flash
   ```
3. Set `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` in `.env`
4. Restart session (`/reset` or relaunch)
5. Try vision_analyze with any image:
   ```
   vision_analyze(image_url="/path/to/image.png", question="What do you see?")
   ```

## Expected behavior

Per the docs ("Image Routing" section), for text-only models `vision_analyze` should fall back to the configured auxiliary vision model (OpenRouter → Gemini Flash) and return a text description.

## Actual behavior

Every call fails with DeepSeeks rejection:
```
Error code: 400 - {"error": {"message": "Failed to deserialize the JSON body into the target type: messages[0]: unknown variant `image_url`, expected `text`"}}
```

This happens regardless of image size (tested: 1.3MB PNG, 213KB JPEG, and ~5KB browser screenshot — all fail identically).

## Configuration verification

```
$ hermes config | grep -A2 auxiliary
◆ Auxiliary Models (overrides)
  Vision        provider=openrouter, model=google/gemini-2.5-flash
```

- `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is set and valid
- `GOOGLE_API_KEY` is also set
- Session was restarted after config change
- Provider was also tried as `google` directly — same result

## Environment

- Hermes version: latest (installed via curl)
- OS: macOS 26.5.2 (Apple Silicon)
- Primary provider: deepseek
- Primary model: deepseek-v4-pro
- Auxiliary vision: openrouter + google/gemini-2.5-flash

## Additional context

The docs state this should work: "For text-only main models... vision_analyze falls back to the legacy path: it asks the configured auxiliary vision model to describe the image and returns the description as plain text."

The same error occurs with `browser_vision` and the CLI image paste path — suggesting the fallback routing is broken at the provider dispatch level, not just in `vision_analyze`.

A user on the CLI with a text-only primary model currently has no working path to vision analysis even with a properly configured auxiliary vision provider and valid API keys.

## Summary

`tests/agent/test_anthropic_adapter.py` is not fully isolated from real Claude Code credentials stored in the macOS Keychain. On a macOS machine with a `Claude Code-credentials` generic password entry, the test file reads the real Keychain credential even when tests monkeypatch `Path.home()` and credential env vars, causing local full-suite failures and potentially printing a real token in pytest assertion diffs.

Debug report: not applicable; this is a test-isolation bug reproduced with a clean checkout and synthetic repro snippets. No private token values are included here.

## Repro

### Real local repro on macOS

1. Use a macOS machine where Claude Code has stored OAuth credentials in Keychain. Verify only the presence of the entry; do not paste the secret value:

   ```bash
   security find-generic-password -s "Claude Code-credentials" -w >/dev/null
   echo $?
   ```

   On the affected machine this exits `0`.

2. From a clean checkout of current main:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent.git
   cd hermes-agent
   git checkout 7e8f50a14
   scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_anthropic_adapter.py -q
   ```

3. Observed local output on `origin/main` at `7e8f50a14`:

   ```text
   14 failed, 159 passed
   ```

   Representative failures, with token contents redacted:

   ```text
   TestResolveAnthropicToken.test_prefers_oauth_token_over_api_key
   E   AssertionError: assert 'sk-ant-oat01-<redacted real keychain token>' == 'sk-ant-oat01-mytoken'
   ```

   ```text
   TestRunOauthSetupToken.test_returns_token_from_credential_files
   E   TypeError: the JSON object must be str, bytes or bytearray, not MagicMock
   ```

### Synthetic repro without private Keychain state

This shows why tests that patch env vars and `Path.home()` are still environment-sensitive: the Keychain reader is independent of `Path.home()`.

```bash
python - <<'PY'
import os
import tempfile
import time
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import patch

from agent.anthropic_adapter import resolve_anthropic_token

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as home:
    os.environ["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"] = "sk-ant-api03-mykey"
    os.environ["ANTHROPIC_TOKEN"] = "[REDACTED:api-key]"
    os.environ.pop("CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN", None)

    fake_keychain_creds = {
        "accessToken": "[REDACTED:api-key]",
        "refreshToken": "refresh-token",
        "expiresAt": int(time.time() * 1000) + 3600_000,
    }

    with patch("agent.anthropic_adapter.Path.home", lambda: Path(home)), patch(
        "agent.anthropic_adapter._read_claude_code_credentials_from_keychain",
        return_value=fake_keychain_creds,
    ):
        print(resolve_anthropic_token())
PY
```

Actual output:

```text
[REDACTED:api-key]
```

The `run_oauth_setup_token()` failures have a second test-isolation path: those tests patch `subprocess.run` for the Claude CLI invocation, but the same patch also intercepts the Keychain `security` command, so the Keychain helper attempts to parse `MagicMock.stdout.strip()` as JSON.

```bash
python - <<'PY'
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

from agent.anthropic_adapter import _read_claude_code_credentials_from_keychain

with patch("platform.system", return_value="Darwin"), patch("subprocess.run") as run:
    run.return_value = MagicMock(returncode=0)
    try:
        print(_read_claude_code_credentials_from_keychain())
    except Exception as exc:
        print(type(exc).__name__, exc)
PY
```

Actual output:

```text
TypeError the JSON object must be str, bytes or bytearray, not MagicMock
```

## Expected

Anthropic adapter tests should be deterministic and independent of the developer machine's real macOS Keychain contents.

Tests that set `ANTHROPIC_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, or a temp `Path.home()` should not be overridden by real Keychain credentials unless the test explicitly opts into that path.

## Actual

On macOS with a real `Claude Code-credentials` Keychain entry:

- `TestResolveAnthropicToken` cases can receive the real Keychain OAuth token instead of the fixture token or `None` expected by the test.
- `TestRunOauthSetupToken` cases can crash with `TypeError: the JSON object must be str, bytes or bytearray, not MagicMock` because their global `subprocess.run` mock also affects the Keychain helper.
- Local full-suite runs fail before unrelated PR validation can truthfully check the all-tests-passed box.

## Root Cause

`agent/anthropic_adapter.py` has a macOS-specific Keychain reader:

- `_read_claude_code_credentials_from_keychain()` shells out to `security find-generic-password -s "Claude Code-credentials" -w`.
- `read_claude_code_credentials()` calls the Keychain reader independently of `Path.home()`.
- `resolve_anthropic_token()` can therefore see real machine-local Claude Code credentials in tests that only monkeypatch env vars and `Path.home()`.

Some tests already patch `read_claude_code_credentials()` or the Keychain reader for this reason, but the affected `TestResolveAnthropicToken` and `TestRunOauthSetupToken` cases do not consistently isolate that path.

## Evidence

- Duplicate search found no open or closed issues/PRs for:
  - `Anthropic adapter keychain test`
  - `Claude Code credentials keychain MagicMock`
  - `read_claude_code_credentials_from_keychain`
- Reproduced on `origin/main` at `7e8f50a14`.
- Reproduced on macOS 26.5.1 with Python 3.11.15.
- The same `tests/agent/test_anthropic_adapter.py` failures occur on a Matrix PR branch that does not touch `agent/anthropic_adapter.py`, confirming this is separate from that PR.

## Proposed Fix

- Add or broaden test fixtures in `tests/agent/test_anthropic_adapter.py` so affected tests patch `_read_claude_code_credentials_from_keychain()` or `read_claude_code_credentials()` when they are not explicitly testing Keychain behavior.
- In `TestRunOauthSetupToken`, avoid a global `subprocess.run` mock catching the Keychain `security` command, or patch the Keychain helper directly in those tests.
- Defensively handle non-string `stdout.strip()` in `_read_claude_code_credentials_from_keychain()` so a mocked subprocess result cannot raise a `TypeError` while parsing JSON.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_anthropic_adapter.py -q` passes on macOS machines with and without a real `Claude Code-credentials` Keychain entry.
- Regression coverage simulates a Keychain credential without reading a real Keychain secret.
- Test failure output never includes a real local Claude Code OAuth token.

labels.name: duplicate

labels.name: comp/dashboard
labels.description: Web dashboard / control panel UI (dashboard/, landing)

items.body:
## Bug

When the dashboard is started with `--host 0.0.0.0` (non-loopback) and `BasicAuthProvider` is the only registered auth provider, accessing the dashboard via a LAN IP (e.g. `http://192.168.x.x:9119`) returns **HTTP 500 Internal Server Error**.

## Root Cause

`BasicAuthProvider` sets `supports_password = True` but does **not** override `supports_session`, so it inherits the base class default `supports_session = True`.

When the auth gate middleware (`_auto_sso_response()` in `dashboard_auth/middleware.py`) sees exactly **one** session provider, it auto-redirects unauthenticated HTML requests to `/auth/login` (the OAuth initiation route). But `BasicAuthProvider.start_login()` raises:

```
NotImplementedError: BasicAuthProvider is password-only; there is no OAuth redirect flow. The login page POSTs to /auth/password-login instead.
```

This is because `BasicAuthProvider` only supports password login (`/auth/password-login`), not the OAuth redirect flow (`/auth/login` → `start_login`).

## Reproduction

1. Configure basic auth in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`:
   ```yaml
   dashboard:
     basic_auth:
       username: admin
       password_hash: "scrypt$..."
   ```

2. Start the dashboard bound to all interfaces:
   ```bash
   hermes dashboard --host 0.0.0.0 --no-open
   ```

3. Access via LAN IP (not 127.0.0.1):
   ```
   curl -v http://192.168.x.x:9119/
   ```

4. Server returns 500 with traceback ending in `NotImplementedError`.

## Expected Behavior

The middleware should not auto-redirect to `/auth/login` when the sole provider is a password-only provider. It should fall through to `/login`, which renders the password form (the login page already handles `supports_password` providers correctly).

## Environment

- Hermes Agent 0.16.0
- Python 3.13
- macOS (Apple Silicon)

## Suggested Fix

In `_auto_sso_response()` (`hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/middleware.py`), filter out `supports_password` providers before checking the count:

```python
providers = list_session_providers()
# Password-only providers (e.g. BasicAuthProvider) don't support the
# OAuth redirect flow — auto-bouncing to /auth/login would hit
# NotImplementedError. Only auto-SSO when the sole provider is OAuth-capable.
providers = [p for p in providers if not getattr(p, "supports_password", False)]
if len(providers) != 1:
    return None
```

Alternatively, `BasicAuthProvider` could set `supports_session = False`, but this would also hide it from the login page (`render_login_html` uses `list_session_providers()`), so the middleware fix is the correct approach.

## Workaround

Patching `middleware.py` as shown above resolves the issue. The fix survives until the next `hermes update` reinstalls site-packages.

items.title: Compression abort can reuse stale in-place compaction state

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
Suggested labels: `type/bug`, `comp/agent`, `comp/gateway`, `P2`, `sweeper:risk-session-state`

## Summary

`_last_compaction_in_place` currently has two meanings: it is both the gateway-visible run signal that an in-place compaction happened, and the latest compression-attempt result used by `conversation_history_after_compression()` to decide whether returned messages are already persisted.

If one compression attempt succeeds in place and a later attempt aborts or returns the original messages unchanged, the run-level signal should stay true, but the latest-attempt flush baseline should be false. Today the later no-op can reuse the stale in-place state and treat unchanged original messages as already compacted/persisted history.

Draft PR with fix: #58629

Debug report: not applicable; reproduced with isolated synthetic repro.

## Repro

1. From a clean checkout of current `main`:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent.git
   cd hermes-agent
   git checkout 7e8f50a14
   ```

2. Run this minimal sequence from the repo root. It simulates a successful in-place compaction followed by an aborted compression attempt on the same agent object:

   ```bash
   python - <<'PY'
   from types import SimpleNamespace

   from agent.conversation_compression import compress_context, conversation_history_after_compression

   class AbortCompressor:
       _last_compress_aborted = False
       _last_summary_error = "summary provider timeout"
       compression_count = 1

       def compress(self, messages, **_kwargs):
           self._last_compress_aborted = True
           return messages

   class SuccessCompressor:
       _last_compress_aborted = False
       _last_summary_error = None
       compression_count = 1
       last_compression_rough_tokens = 0
       last_prompt_tokens = 0
       last_completion_tokens = 0
       awaiting_real_usage_after_compression = False

       def compress(self, _messages, **_kwargs):
           return [{"role": "user", "content": "[summary]"}]

   class FakeSessionDB:
       def try_acquire_compression_lock(self, *_args, **_kwargs):
           return True
       def release_compression_lock(self, *_args, **_kwargs):
           pass
       def archive_and_compact(self, _session_id, _messages):
           pass
       def update_system_prompt(self, _session_id, _system_prompt):
           pass

   def make_agent(compressor):
       return SimpleNamespace(
           _last_compaction_in_place=False,
           _compression_feasibility_checked=True,
           compression_in_place=True,
           context_compressor=compressor,
           session_id="sess-1",
           model="test-model",
           tools=None,
           platform=None,
           _gateway_session_key=None,
           log_prefix="",
           _session_db=FakeSessionDB(),
           _memory_manager=None,
           _todo_store=SimpleNamespace(format_for_injection=lambda: ""),
           _cached_system_prompt="cached-system",
           _last_compression_summary_warning=None,
           _build_system_prompt=lambda system_message: f"system:{system_message}",
           _invalidate_system_prompt=lambda: None,
           commit_memory_session=lambda _messages: None,
           _emit_status=lambda _message: None,
           _emit_warning=lambda _message: None,
       )

   messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "keep this"}]
   agent = make_agent(SuccessCompressor())
   compressed, _ = compress_context(agent, messages, "system")
   print("after_success_run_flag", agent._last_compaction_in_place)
   print("after_success_history", conversation_history_after_compression(agent, compressed))

   agent.context_compressor = AbortCompressor()
   returned, _ = compress_context(agent, messages, "system")
   print("after_abort_run_flag", agent._last_compaction_in_place)
   print("after_abort_history", conversation_history_after_compression(agent, returned))

   assert agent._last_compaction_in_place is True
   assert conversation_history_after_compression(agent, returned) is None
   PY
   ```

3. Observed output on `origin/main` at `7e8f50a14`:

   ```text
   after_success_run_flag True
   after_success_history [{'role': 'user', 'content': '[summary]'}]
   after_abort_run_flag True
   after_abort_history [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'keep this'}]
   AssertionError
   ```

## Expected

After the aborted/no-op compression attempt:

- the run-level signal should remain true if an earlier in-place compaction succeeded during the run, so gateway/session code can still re-baseline transcript handling; and
- `conversation_history_after_compression()` should return `None` for the aborted attempt because the returned original messages were not just compacted and persisted in place.

## Actual

`conversation_history_after_compression()` reads the stale `_last_compaction_in_place` flag and returns `list(messages)` for the aborted/no-op attempt. That makes the unchanged original messages look like an already-persisted compacted baseline.

## Root Cause

`agent/conversation_compression.py` uses `_last_compaction_in_place` for two different lifetimes:

- run-level gateway/session state: an in-place compaction happened at some point in the current turn; and
- latest compression attempt state: the current `compress_context()` result was persisted via in-place compaction.

Those diverge when a successful in-place compaction is followed by a failed or no-op compression attempt.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on `origin/main` at `7e8f50a14`.
- Duplicate/related sweep checked `_last_compaction_in_place`, `conversation_history_after_compression`, `compression abort no-op in-place`, and `last compression attempt in place` across open and closed issues/PRs.
- Related but not duplicate:
  - #50098 fixed gateway/slash callers reading the config flag instead of `_last_compaction_in_place`.
  - #58155 increased reliance on `conversation_history_after_compression()` for mid-turn compaction.
  - #58081 / #58133 cover Responses API ResponseStore bloat, not latest-attempt vs run-level flag lifetime.
- Draft fix #58629 passes focused compression/gateway validation.

## Proposed Fix

Split the state:

- keep `_last_compaction_in_place` as the run-level signal read by gateway/session code;
- add a latest-attempt signal for `conversation_history_after_compression()`; and
- reset the run-level signal at the start of each `run_conversation()` call so reused agents do not leak old compaction state across turns.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A regression test covers successful in-place compaction followed by an aborted/no-op compression attempt.
- `conversation_history_after_compression()` returns `None` for the aborted/no-op attempt while the run-level in-place signal remains true.
- A reused agent starts a new `run_conversation()` call with stale run-level in-place state cleared.
- Existing focused compression, persistence, and gateway session tests continue to pass.

items.title: MoA auxiliary tasks (provider: auto) send preset name as model ID → HTTP 400

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug

When MoA (Mixture-of-Agents) is the active main provider, auxiliary tasks (title generation, compression, vision, session search, etc.) configured with `provider: auto` (the default) fail with HTTP 400 — the MoA preset name is sent as the model ID instead of the real aggregator model.

**Visible symptom** (from `agent.log`):
```
Auxiliary title_generation: using auto (default) at http://172.24.48.1:18089/v1/
WARNING agent.title_generator: Title generation failed: Error code: 400 - {"error":"...用户对该模型无权限...TM.00001005..."}
```
Note `using auto (default)` — `"default"` is the MoA preset name, not a valid model ID.

All auxiliary tasks using `provider: auto` (title_generation, compression, vision, web_extract, session_search, curator, mcp, skills_hub, monitor, profile_describer, triage_specifier, kanban_decomposer, approval, tts_audio_tags) are affected when MoA is the main provider.

## Root Cause

In `agent/auxiliary_client.py`, `resolve_provider_client()` has a model pre-fill step before the auto branch:

```python
# Line ~4005
if not model:
    model = _get_aux_model_for_provider(provider) or _read_main_model() or model
```

When MoA is active, `set_runtime_main(provider="moa", model="default", ...)` sets the process-global `_RUNTIME_MAIN_MODEL = "default"` (the preset name — MoA has no real HTTP endpoint). So `_read_main_model()` returns `"default"` and `model` gets pre-filled with it.

Then in the auto branch:

```python
# Line ~4150
if provider == "auto":
    client, resolved = _resolve_auto(main_runtime=main_runtime, task=task)
    ...
    final_model = model or resolved   # ← model="default" is truthy → final_model="default"
```

`_resolve_auto()` **correctly** resolves MoA → aggregator and returns the real model ID (e.g. `"maas-glm-5.2-aliyun"`). This resolution was added by #53827 (merged 2026-06-27) via the `if main_provider == "moa":` block inside `_resolve_auto()`. But `final_model = model or resolved` picks the pre-filled `model="default"` (truthy) over the correct `resolved` value, **overriding** #53827's fix.

The request goes out with `model="default"` → the backend rejects it (400 / TM.00001005 / "not a valid model ID").

## Why PR #53827 Didn't Fully Fix This

#53827 fixed `_resolve_auto()` to return the correct aggregator model. But the bug is one level up: `resolve_provider_client()`'s auto branch overrides `_resolve_auto()`'s return value with the pre-filled `model`. The pre-fill comes from `_read_main_model()`, which returns the MoA preset name — a value that is truthy but not a valid model ID for any real endpoint.

| Layer | Fixed by | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `_resolve_auto()` MoA→aggregator resolution | #53827 | ✅ Merged |
| `resolve_provider_client()` auto branch model override | — | ❌ Not fixed on `main` |

## Proposed Fix

One-line change in `resolve_provider_client()`'s auto branch (`agent/auxiliary_client.py` ~line 4150):

```diff
-        final_model = model or resolved
+        # _resolve_auto() already handles MoA preset → aggregator resolution
+        # (PR #53827). Its returned ``resolved`` model is the real model ID
+        # the endpoint accepts. The pre-filled ``model`` from
+        # _read_main_model() may be a MoA preset name (e.g. "default") that
+        # is NOT a valid model ID — using it overrides _resolve_auto's
+        # correct resolution and causes HTTP 400. Prefer ``resolved`` so
+        # the auto-detect chain's answer wins; ``model`` remains as
+        # fallback when _resolve_auto returns None (non-MoA fallthrough).
+        final_model = resolved or model
```

`resolved` (from `_resolve_auto()`, which handles MoA→aggregator) takes precedence. `model` remains as fallback for the non-MoA fallthrough case where `_resolve_auto` returns `None`.

## Verification

### Before fix (live `hermes chat --provider moa -m default`)

`agent.log`:
```
2026-07-05 10:44:22,183 INFO agent.auxiliary_client: Auxiliary title_generation: using auto (default) at http://172.24.48.1:18089/v1/
2026-07-05 10:44:22,635 WARNING agent.title_generator: Title generation failed: Error code: 400 - {"error":"{\"text\":\"[DONE]\",\"error\":{\"error_msg\":\"用户对该模型无权限...\",\"error_code\":\"TM.00001005\"}}"}
```

### After fix (same command)

`agent.log`:
```
2026-07-05 11:21:56,574 INFO agent.auxiliary_client: Auxiliary auto-detect: using main provider custom:codeagent (maas-glm-5.2-aliyun)
2026-07-05 11:21:56,576 INFO agent.auxiliary_client: Auxiliary title_generation: using auto (maas-glm-5.2-aliyun) at http://172.24.48.1:18089/v1/
```
No error follows. Model correctly resolved to aggregator's `maas-glm-5.2-aliyun` instead of preset name `"default"`.

### Direct resolution test

```python
from agent.auxiliary_client import set_runtime_main, resolve_provider_client
set_runtime_main(provider="moa", model="default", base_url="moa://local",
                 api_key="moa-virtual-provider", api_mode="chat_completions")
client, model = resolve_provider_client("auto", None, task="title_generation")
# Before:  model = "default" (preset name → 400)
# After:   model = "maas-glm-5.2-aliyun" (aggregator model → works)
```

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: latest `main` (verified `final_model = model or resolved` still present at line 4150 on `main`)
- Provider: MoA with custom aggregator (`custom:codeagent` → `maas-glm-5.2-aliyun`)
- Platform: WSL / CLI

## Related

- #53827 (merged) — fixed `_resolve_auto()` MoA→aggregator resolution, but the override bug in `resolve_provider_client()` remains
- #54021 (closed/duplicate) — duplicate of #53827
- #56691 (open) — different path: fixes `_resolve_task_provider_model` for explicit `auxiliary.<task>.provider: moa` config, not the `auto` path
- #57283 (open) — desktop app variant of the same preset-name-as-model-id symptom

items.title: fix(plugins): entry-point plugins missing from 'hermes plugins list'

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug

`hermes plugins list` does not show pip-installed plugins that register via the `hermes_agent.plugins` entry-point group. The plugins are **loaded and active** — they just don't appear in the list output.

## Root cause

There are two separate plugin discovery paths:

1. **`PluginManager.discover_and_load()`** (`hermes_cli/plugins.py`) — the **actual loader**. Scans directories AND `importlib.metadata` entry points (via `_scan_entry_points`). Entry-point plugins are discovered, loaded, and registered correctly. ✅

2. **`_discover_all_plugins()`** (`hermes_cli/plugins_cmd.py`) — the **display path** for `hermes plugins list`. Only scans `bundled` and `user` directories. Does NOT scan entry points. ❌

So a pip-installed plugin like [rtk-hermes](https://github.com/ogallotti/rtk-hermes) (entry point `rtk-rewrite -> rtk_hermes`) is loaded by the gateway and actively rewriting commands, but is invisible in `hermes plugins list` — including `--json` and `--plain` output.

## Reproduction

```bash
pip install rtk-hermes        # registers hermes_agent.plugins entry point
# add rtk-rewrite to plugins.enabled in config.yaml
hermes gateway restart
hermes plugins list           # rtk-rewrite NOT shown
hermes plugins list --plain   # rtk-rewrite NOT shown
hermes plugins list --json    # rtk-rewrite NOT shown
```

Verify the plugin IS loaded:

```python
from hermes_cli.plugins import PluginManager
pm = PluginManager()
pm.discover_and_load()
for key, lp in pm._plugins.items():
    if 'rtk' in key.lower():
        print(f"KEY={key} enabled={lp.enabled} error={lp.error} source={lp.manifest.source}")
        # Output: KEY=rtk-rewrite enabled=True error=None source=entrypoint
```

## Fix

`_discover_all_plugins()` in `hermes_cli/plugins_cmd.py` needs to also scan entry points, mirroring `PluginManager._scan_entry_points`.

### Changes

**`hermes_cli/plugins_cmd.py`** — add `_discover_entry_point_plugins()` and call it from `_discover_all_plugins()`:

```python
def _discover_entry_point_plugins() -> list:
    """Discover pip-installed plugins via importlib.metadata entry points.
    Mirrors PluginManager._scan_entry_points so that plugins distributed
    as pip packages (e.g. rtk-hermes) show up in hermes plugins list.
    """
    import importlib.metadata

    entries: list = []
    try:
        eps = importlib.metadata.entry_points()
        group = "hermes_agent.plugins"
        if hasattr(eps, "select"):
            group_eps = eps.select(group=group)
        elif isinstance(eps, dict):
            group_eps = eps.get(group, [])
        else:
            group_eps = [ep for ep in eps if ep.group == group]

        for ep in group_eps:
            version = ""
            description = ""
            try:
                dist = importlib.metadata.metadata(ep.dist.name)
                version = dist.get("Version", "") or ""
                summary = dist.get("Summary", "")
                description = summary if summary else ""
            except Exception:
                pass
            entries.append(
                (ep.name, version, description, "entrypoint", Path(ep.value), ep.name)
            )
    except Exception:
        pass
    return entries
```

Then in `_discover_all_plugins()`, after the directory scans:

```python
    # Pip / entry-point plugins (mirror PluginManager._scan_entry_points)
    for entry in _discover_entry_point_plugins():
        name, version, description, source, path, key = entry
        if key not in seen:
            seen[key] = entry
```

**Tests** — 3 existing tests patched to mock `_discover_entry_point_plugins` (return `[]`), plus 2 new tests:

- `test_discover_entry_point_plugins_returns_tuples` — verifies 6-tuple format
- `test_discover_all_plugins_includes_entry_points` — verifies entry-points appear in discovery

## Verification

After applying the patch:

```
$ hermes plugins list --plain | grep rtk
enabled      entrypoint 1.2.3    rtk-rewrite
```

All 84 plugins now show (83 directory-based + 1 entry-point). No regressions — 27/27 plugin tests pass.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: latest main (commit 7e8f50a14)
- OS: Windows 10
- Python: 3.11.15
- Plugin tested: rtk-hermes v1.2.3 (pip-installed, entry point `hermes_agent.plugins`)

## Bug Description
The QQ bot adapter fails to connect to the gateway. During both initial startup and reconnection, the gateway calls adapter.connect() with the argument is_reconnect=True. However, QQAdapter.connect() does not support this parameter, which triggers a TypeError and puts the adapter into an infinite retry loop.

## Error Log
ERROR gateway.run: ✗ qqbot error: QQAdapter.connect() got an unexpected keyword argument 'is_reconnect'
WARNING gateway.run: Gateway started with no connected platforms — 1 platform(s) queued for retry: qqbot
WARNING gateway.run: Reconnect qqbot error: ... next retry in 60s
WARNING gateway.run: Reconnect qqbot error: ... next retry in 120s

## Root Cause
The base class PlatformAdapterBase located at gateway/platforms/base.py line 2864 defines the abstract method as below:
@abstractmethod
async def connect(self, *, is_reconnect: bool = False) -> bool:

But the connect method in QQAdapter (gateway/platforms/qqbot/adapter.py) is only defined as:
async def connect(self) -> bool:

The gateway invokes adapter.connect(is_reconnect=is_reconnect) in two places within gateway/run.py for cold boot and reconnection respectively. The QQ adapter cannot recognize this keyword argument and throws an error.

## Fix Solution
Update the signature of QQAdapter.connect() to accept the is_reconnect parameter:
async def connect(self, *, is_reconnect: bool = False) -> bool:

No changes to the internal logic are required; the is_reconnect argument can remain unused. This implementation pattern is consistent with other adapters such as webhook.py.

## Affected Code File
https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/gateway/platforms/qqbot/adapter.py

## Additional Context
All other platform adapters should be audited. Any adapter that overrides connect() without the is_reconnect keyword argument will encounter the identical issue.

items.title: Discord: fail-closed auth default is silent + setup wizard prints inverted warning
items.body:
## Summary

Discord's fail-closed authorization default (correct per SECURITY.md §2.6) has no user-facing feedback and a stale setup-wizard warning, producing a confusing "connected but every message is silently dropped" experience.

This is the real UX bug underneath #58568 / #58583. The security default itself is correct and stays — this issue is purely about surfacing *why* traffic is being denied and how to open it up.

## Two defects

**1. Silent message drop (no log)**
`plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py:1095`

```python
if not self._is_allowed_user(...):
    return
```

A bare `return` — no log line. The bot shows "✓ discord connected", `on_message` fires, and every message vanishes with zero operator feedback. Reporter's exact symptom: "No error is logged."

Proposed: a **one-time** warning (rate-limited / once-per-process, not per-message) when the first message is denied under a no-allowlist-configured fail-closed state, naming the fix: "Discord messages are being denied because no allowlist is configured. Set DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS / DISCORD_ALLOWED_ROLES / DISCORD_ALLOWED_CHANNELS, or DISCORD_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true for open access."

**2. Stale, inverted setup-wizard warnings**
`plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py:7585` and `:7618`

```python
print_info("⚠️  Discord has no user allowlist - anyone can use your bot!")
...
print_info("⚠️  No allowlist set - anyone in servers with your bot can use it!")
```

These describe the *old* fail-open behavior. The code now fails **closed** — with no allowlist, *nobody* can use the bot. The warnings should be corrected to reflect fail-closed and point at `DISCORD_ALLOW_ALL_USERS`.

## Non-goals

- Do **not** revert the fail-closed default (that's the SECURITY.md §2.6 policy; see #58583 close comment).

## Refs

- Reported behavior: #58568
- Rejected revert PR: #58583
- Security policy: SECURITY.md §2.6 rule #2
- Deliberate fail-closed commit: `bb304b491`

## Bug Report

**Hermes version:** v0.18.0 (2026.7.1) · upstream 10423297

### Symptom
Async delegation results (`delegate_task`) are delivered to the **currently active session** instead of the **session that dispatched them**.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Open session A (topic: Zeus catalog analysis)
2. Dispatch subagents via `delegate_task` from session A at 13:51
3. Switch to session B (topic: Ollama/KB discussion)
4. Subagents complete — results land in **session B** instead of session A

### Expected behavior
Subagent results should always return to the session that dispatched them, regardless of which session is active when they complete.

### Actual behavior
Results are routed to whichever session is the active recipient at completion time.

### Impact
- Cross-contamination between unrelated sessions
- User loses context on long-running delegations
- Impossible to run async delegation while working on something else in another thread

### Likely cause
The delivery router uses the current active `source` at completion time rather than the dispatching session's ID. The dispatching session ID should be captured at dispatch time and used for delivery.

items.body:
## Description

When a custom provider is defined under `providers:` in config.yaml with a unique model name (not shared with any built-in provider), the desktop Settings → Model selector does not correctly map the model to its configured provider. Instead, it falls back to OpenRouter, which doesn't have the model — resulting in `HTTP 400: <model> is not a valid model ID`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Define a custom provider with a unique model name in config.yaml:
```yaml
providers:
  longcat:
    api_key: ${LONGCAT_API_KEY}
    base_url: https://api.longcat.chat/openai
    model: LongCat-2.0
    name: LongCat
    models:
      - id: LongCat-2.0
        context_length: 1048576
```

2. Open Desktop Settings → Model, select "LongCat-2.0"
3. Start a new session and send a message

## Expected behavior

Hermes should use `providers.longcat.base_url` (`https://api.longcat.chat/openai`) to route the request.

## Actual behavior

Hermes routes the request through OpenRouter:

```
provider=custom base_url=https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 model=LongCat-2.0
→ HTTP 400: LongCat-2.0 is not a valid model ID
```

## Evidence

From agent.log:
```
2026-07-05 14:15:50,035 INFO: Streaming failed before delivery: Error code: 400
2026-07-05 14:15:50,036 WARNING: API call failed (attempt 1/3) error_type=BadRequestError provider=custom base_url=https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 model=LongCat-2.0
```

The desktop model selector resolves models by searching built-in provider model lists only. Custom provider models under `providers:<name>.models` are not included in this search. When a unique model name is not found, it defaults to OpenRouter.

## Workaround

```
/model --provider longcat LongCat-2.0
```

This bypasses the desktop selector and directly writes the provider mapping.

## Impact

Custom providers with unique model names are unusable through the desktop UI. Providers with shared model names (e.g., `deepseek-v4-flash` which exists across multiple providers) are unaffected.

## Version

hermes-agent desktop GUI on macOS, latest as of 2026-07-05

# Bug: Cron delivery fails with `RuntimeError('cannot schedule new futures after interpreter shutdown')`

## Summary

Every LLM-driven cron job delivery fails with `RuntimeError('cannot schedule new futures after interpreter shutdown')` when the job targets a Telegram delivery channel. The error occurs because `agent.close()` inside `run_job()`'s finally block tears down async resources before `_deliver_result()` runs in `run_one_job()`.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.17.0+
- Linux (Proxmox VE)
- Single shared `hermes-gateway.service` (multiplex_profiles=true, 5 profiles)
- Python 3.13

## Reproduction

1. Create an LLM-driven cron job (not `no_agent`) with `deliver` targeting a Telegram group/topic
2. Let the job complete — it will produce output successfully
3. Delivery fails with the error

## Root Cause Analysis

The call chain in `cron/scheduler.py`:

1. `run_one_job()` calls `run_job(job)` (line 3117)
2. `run_job()` runs the agent in a `ThreadPoolExecutor` (line 2857)
3. `run_job()`'s `finally` block (line 2892) shuts down the pool, then calls `agent.close()` (line 3073) which tears down the agent's async httpx clients
4. `run_job()` returns to `run_one_job()`
5. `run_one_job()` calls `_deliver_result(job, ..., loop=loop)` (line 3144) — **after** the agent has been closed
6. `_deliver_result()` tries `safe_schedule_threadsafe(router._deliver_to_platform(...), loop)` (line 1505)
7. `safe_schedule_threadsafe()` calls `asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(coro, loop)` (async_utils.py line 63)
8. This fails with `RuntimeError('cannot schedule new futures after interpreter shutdown')` because the loop's executor has been marked for shutdown during `agent.close()`

The fallback standalone path (line 1690) also fails because `asyncio.run()` in a fresh thread hits the same torn-down executor state.

## Evidence

### Logs (every cron run since 03/07/2026)

```
Jul 05 14:08:22 hermesagent-svr python[2594839]: ERROR cron.scheduler: Job 'cron_model_governor_001': delivery error: Telegram send failed: Unknown error in HTTP implementation: RuntimeError('cannot schedule new futures after interpreter shutdown')
```

Also affects Hindsight memory plugin:
```
Jul 03 21:21:10 hermesagent-svr python[1863546]: WARNING plugins.memory.hindsight: Hindsight retain failed: cannot schedule new futures after shutdown
Jul 03 21:21:10 hermesagent-svr python[1863546]:     raise RuntimeError('cannot schedule new futures after shutdown')
```

### Affected jobs

- `_Cron Model Governor` (cron_model_governor_001) — every run since 04/07
- `_Cron Model Assessment` (dc357af70533, now deleted) — every run since 03/07
- `Self-Evolution - All Skills Nightly` (601710fe8b42) — 05/07 run

### Key observation

The error message differs slightly:
- `"cannot schedule new futures after interpreter shutdown"` — from `asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe()`
- `"cannot schedule new futures after shutdown"` — from a `ThreadPoolExecutor` directly

Both indicate the same root cause: executor shutdown ordering.

## Suggested Fix

Move `_deliver_result()` **inside** `run_job()`, before the `finally` block that calls `agent.close()`. Alternatively, defer `agent.close()` until after delivery completes.

Current order:
```
run_job():
  finally:
    _cron_pool.shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True)  # line 2892
    agent.close()  # line 3073 — tears down async clients
    cleanup_stale_async_clients()  # line 3082

run_one_job():
  run_job(job)  # agent already closed when this returns
  _deliver_result(job, ..., loop=loop)  # line 3144 — FAILS: loop executor torn down
```

Proposed order:
```
run_job():
  # ... agent execution ...
  _deliver_result(job, ..., loop=loop)  # deliver BEFORE cleanup
  finally:
    _cron_pool.shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True)
    agent.close()
    cleanup_stale_async_clients()
```

Or in `run_one_job()`, move delivery before the cleanup:
```
run_one_job():
  success, output, final_response, error = run_job(job, skip_cleanup=True)
  _deliver_result(job, ...)  # deliver while agent resources still alive
  run_job_cleanup(job)  # separate cleanup step
```

## Workaround

Converting the cron job to `no_agent=True` (script-only) avoids the issue entirely — no agent is created, so `agent.close()` is not called, and the loop's executor remains healthy for delivery.

## Files

- `cron/scheduler.py` — `run_one_job()` (line 3087), `run_job()` (line ~2800-3084), `_deliver_result()` (line 1220), `safe_schedule_threadsafe()` usage (line 1505)
- `agent/async_utils.py` — `safe_schedule_threadsafe()` (line 34)
- `gateway/run.py` — cron ticker start (line 20050), passes `asyncio.get_running_loop()` to `tick()`

items.body:
## Bug Description

`hermes update` has been failing **consistently for over 1.5 months** on Windows. The update process cannot replace `hermes.exe` because Windows locks a running executable, blocking both the git-based `pip install -e .` and the ZIP fallback path.

## Environment

- **OS**: Windows 10
- **Hermes version**: v0.17.0 (2026.6.19, 41c85fb9)
- **Install location** (Desktop app): `C:\Users\av_ch\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent\venv\Scripts\hermes.exe`
- **Also installed at** (git clone): `C:\Users\av_ch\.hermes\hermes-agent\venv\Scripts\hermes.exe`
- **Update shows**: "1 commit behind - run 'hermes update'"

## Logs (hermes-update.log)

Every update attempt since **2026-05-20** has failed with the same core issue:

### Pattern 1 — Running executable blocked (most common, ~12+ attempts)

```
✗ Another hermes.exe is running:
    PID 26808  hermes.exe

  Updating now would fail to overwrite ...hermes.exe because
  Windows blocks REPLACE on a running executable.
```

This blocks even when only the Hermes Desktop app is running (and no REPL sessions or gateway).

### Pattern 2 — pip install fails -> ZIP fallback -> still blocked

```
→ Updating Python dependencies...
  ⚠ Could not quarantine hermes.exe: [WinError 32] file in use
  ⚠ Optional extras failed, reinstalling base dependencies...
⚠ Git update failed: Command `uv pip install -e .` returned non-zero exit status 2.
→ Falling back to ZIP download...
→ Downloading latest version...
→ Extracting...
✗ ZIP update failed: [WinError 5] Access Denied: ...\chrome_100_percent.pak
```

Git pull works fine, but `uv pip install -e .` fails because it needs to quarantine the running `hermes.exe`.

### Pattern 3 — Desktop app files locked during ZIP

```
✗ ZIP update failed: [WinError 5] Access Denied: ...\release\win-unpacked\chrome_100_percent.pak
```

### Pattern 4 — "Scheduled replacement on next reboot" never takes effect

```
⚠ hermes.exe is locked by another process; scheduled replacement on next reboot.
```

The replacement never seems to take effect on subsequent updates.

## Root Cause

Windows does not allow **renaming or overwriting a running .exe file**. The update script tries to:
1. `os.rename(hermes.exe, hermes.exe.old.timestamp)` — fails with WinError 32
2. When that fails, `uv pip install -e .` cannot complete because pip also cannot write the exe
3. ZIP fallback downloads code files, but the `hermes.exe` shim still can't be replaced

The Hermes Desktop app (Electron) starts `hermes.exe` at launch, so during normal Desktop usage the file is always locked.

## Suggested Fixes

1. **Use MOVEFILE_DELAY_UNTIL_REBOOT** (via ctypes/MoveFileEx on Windows) to schedule exe replacement, then write a new launcher stub to a temp path
2. **Download new hermes.exe to hermes.exe.new** and use a launcher shim that atomically swaps on next cold start
3. **Auto-kill then restart**: during update, kill all hermes.exe PIDs, do the swap, then restart
4. **At minimum**: implement `--force` flag that kills hermes.exe PIDs before updating (mentioned in error messages but not implemented)

The `--force` flag referenced in the error message ("Override with `hermes update --force`") is **not implemented** — passing it gives an "unknown flag" error.

items.body:
Feature Request: Per-subagent model override in delegate_task

## Problem
`delegation.model` / `delegation.provider` in config.yaml currently applies globally to ALL subagents. There is no way to route different subagent roles to different models.

## Why This Matters
The master-worker pattern (see: OpenCode + oh-my-opencode-slim's Solo orchestration model) demonstrates that different subagent roles need different models:

| Role | Model | Why |
|------|-------|-----|
| explorer / editor | fast model (flash) | File search and code edits are mechanical tasks — no deep reasoning needed |
| verify / reviewer | expert model (pro) | Adversarial verification and code review need high reasoning quality |
| oracle / researcher | expert model (pro) | Root-cause analysis and complex planning |
| observer | vision model | Multimodal tasks need specialized capabilities |

Without per-task model override, you either pay pro prices for flash tasks, or compromise quality on tasks that need reasoning.

## Proposed API
Add optional `model` and `provider` fields to each task in `delegate_task`:

```
delegate_task(tasks=[
    {"goal": "Explore codebase for auth logic", "model": "deepseek-v4-flash"},
    {"goal": "Verify the refactored code runs", "model": "deepseek-v4-pro"},
    {"goal": "Screenshot the dashboard", "model": "kimi-k2.5", "provider": "opencode-go"},
])
```

- Per-task `model` overrides `delegation.model` (config-level default)
- Per-task `provider` overrides `delegation.provider`
- If omitted, fall back to config → parent model
- Same config.yaml schema, just resolved per-task

## Related
- `delegation.model` / `delegation.provider` in config.yaml already exists but is global
- Per-task `toolsets` already exists — model routing would follow the same per-task pattern
- This is one of 3 gaps identified vs OpenCode Solo pattern:
  1. ~~Per-subagent model routing~~ ← this issue
  2. Built-in verify/review agent patterns (can be done via skill)
  3. Per-subagent toolset restrictions (already exists via `toolsets` parameter)

items.title: [Bug]: Groq STT ignores provider-specific model in config.yaml
items.body:
## Bug Description

Groq STT model selection appears to ignore provider-specific configuration in `config.yaml`. For other STT providers, `transcribe_audio(..., model=None)` reads a provider-namespaced model from `stt.<provider>.model`, but the Groq branch falls back directly to `DEFAULT_GROQ_STT_MODEL`, which is currently derived from the `STT_GROQ_MODEL` environment variable.

That makes Groq different from OpenAI/Mistral/local/plugin STT configuration and forces a non-secret behavioral setting into env instead of `config.yaml`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure STT with Groq and a provider-specific model:

```yaml
stt:
  enabled: true
  provider: groq
  groq:
    model: whisper-large-v3
```

2. Ensure `STT_GROQ_MODEL` is unset.
3. Trigger voice transcription through gateway or call `tools.transcription_tools.transcribe_audio(path, model=None)`.

## Expected Behavior

Groq should use `stt.groq.model` when no explicit `model=...` argument is passed, matching the existing provider-specific config pattern:

- `stt.local.model` for local/local_command
- `stt.openai.model` for OpenAI
- `stt.mistral.model` for Mistral
- `stt.<plugin>.model` for transcription plugins

Explicit caller-provided `model=...` should still win over config.

## Actual Behavior

The Groq branch currently ignores `stt.groq.model` and uses `DEFAULT_GROQ_STT_MODEL`:

```python
if provider == "groq":
    model_name = model or DEFAULT_GROQ_STT_MODEL
    return _transcribe_groq(file_path, model_name)
```

`DEFAULT_GROQ_STT_MODEL` is initialized from env:

```python
DEFAULT_GROQ_STT_MODEL = os.getenv("STT_GROQ_MODEL", "whisper-large-v3-turbo")
```

So the only current way to select `whisper-large-v3` by default for Groq is to set `STT_GROQ_MODEL`.

## Affected Component

Configuration (`config.yaml`, `.env`, `hermes setup`) and gateway voice/STT paths that call `transcribe_audio()`.

## Root Cause Analysis

In `tools/transcription_tools.py`:

- `DEFAULT_GROQ_STT_MODEL` is env-derived near the top of the file.
- `transcribe_audio()` handles Groq as `model or DEFAULT_GROQ_STT_MODEL`.
- The function does not read `stt_config.get("groq", {}).get("model")`.

This is inconsistent with adjacent provider branches and with transcription plugin tests that already assert provider-namespaced `stt.<provider>.model` behavior.

## Proposed Fix

Make the Groq branch mirror the other providers:

```python
if provider == "groq":
    groq_cfg = stt_config.get("groq", {})
    model_name = model or groq_cfg.get("model", DEFAULT_GROQ_STT_MODEL)
    return _transcribe_groq(file_path, model_name)
```

A focused regression test should verify:

1. `stt.groq.model` is used when `model=None`.
2. Explicit `model=...` still overrides config.
3. Env default remains a fallback when config is absent.

## Environment

Observed on current upstream-derived checkout after updating to latest `main` as of 2026-07-05. The issue is visible from source inspection and can be reproduced without a full debug report.

items.body:
Related to #58748.

## Bug Description

When the base Python interpreter for Hermes's uv-created venv is missing, the desktop repair flow initially reuses the broken venv instead of detecting that the uv trampoline cannot spawn its target and forcing a fresh venv rebuild.

The desktop error loop showed:

```text
[hermes] [boot] Using existing Hermes Python at <user-home>\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent\venv\Scripts\python.exe
[hermes] [boot] Starting Hermes backend via existing Hermes Python ...
[hermes] Waiting for Hermes backend to launch
[hermes] error: uv trampoline failed to spawn Python child process
[hermes] Caused by: entity not found (os error 2)
[hermes] Hermes backend exited (1)
```

The `venv\Scripts\python.exe` file existed, so the bootstrapper treated the venv as reusable. But that executable was only a uv trampoline; its base interpreter, referenced from `venv\pyvenv.cfg`, had been deleted. Reusing the venv therefore failed every time.

The user recovered by manually renaming:

```text
<user-home>\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent\venv
```

to a backup name, forcing Repair install to build a fresh venv.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have Hermes installed on Windows with a uv-created venv at:

   ```text
   <user-home>\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent\venv
   ```

2. Remove the base interpreter referenced by:

   ```bash
   grep "^home" "$HOME/AppData/Local/hermes/hermes-agent/venv/pyvenv.cfg"
   ```

3. Launch Hermes Desktop.
4. Click Retry or Repair install.

## Expected Behavior

Repair install should detect that the venv's `Scripts\python.exe` trampoline cannot actually execute, or that `pyvenv.cfg`'s `home =` path no longer exists, and automatically rebuild the venv.

A healthy repair flow should do something like:

1. Check whether `venv\Scripts\python.exe -V` succeeds.
2. Check whether `venv\pyvenv.cfg` exists and its `home =` path exists.
3. If either check fails, rename or remove the broken venv and create a new one.
4. Show a clear message such as:

   ```text
   Existing Hermes venv references a missing base Python; rebuilding venv.
   ```

## Actual Behavior

Repair reused the existing venv because `venv\Scripts\python.exe` existed, then failed repeatedly with:

```text
uv trampoline failed to spawn Python child process
Caused by: entity not found (os error 2)
```

Manual intervention was required to rename/delete the venv before Repair could proceed.

## Related Recovery Observations

After forcing the venv rebuild, the user encountered two additional repair-stage blockers:

1. Repository divergence:

   ```text
   fatal: Not possible to fast-forward, aborting.
   git pull failed (exit 128)
   ```

   This was fixed with:

   ```bash
   cd "$HOME/AppData/Local/hermes/hermes-agent"
   git fetch origin
   git reset --hard origin/main
   git clean -fd
   ```

2. Windows encoding issue during config-template sync:

   ```text
   stdout read error: stream did not contain valid UTF-8
   install.ps1 -Stage config-templates produced no JSON result frame (exit=Some(0))
   ```

   This was fixed by setting:

   ```powershell
   setx PYTHONUTF8 1
   setx PYTHONIOENCODING utf-8
   ```

Those are separate issues, but the primary repair UX bug here is that the installer reused a broken uv-trampoline venv instead of validating and rebuilding it.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 10
- Hermes surface: Desktop app repair/bootstrap flow
- Python management: uv-managed Python / uv trampoline venv
- Hermes runtime path:

  ```text
  <user-home>\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent\venv\Scripts\python.exe
  ```

- Error:

  ```text
  uv trampoline failed to spawn Python child process
  Caused by: entity not found (os error 2)
  ```

## Proposed Fix

Enhance bootstrap/repair validation so `Using existing Hermes Python` only happens after verifying the venv's Python can actually execute. If execution fails with the uv trampoline missing-target error, Repair should automatically rebuild the venv instead of requiring the user to discover and rename `venv` manually.

Potential checks:

```text
venv\Scripts\python.exe -V
```

and/or:

```text
read venv\pyvenv.cfg
verify `home = ...` exists
```

If either fails, mark the venv invalid and rebuild.

items.title: Compression can drop the only user-role message, causing a non-retryable "No user query found in messages" crash — hits kanban workers hard

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Summary

`agent/context_compressor.py` has an existing guard (`_ensure_last_user_message_in_tail` / `_find_last_user_message_idx`, built for #10896 and hardened for #22523) meant to guarantee the most recent user-role message always survives compression. In practice, on a `hermes kanban` worker session, this guard did not prevent the compressed message list from ending up with **zero user-role messages**, which then gets rejected outright by an OpenAI-compatible backend (vLLM/Qwen) with a **non-retryable** `400 Bad Request: No user query found in messages`. The worker crashes immediately and can never recover on retry, because every resumed attempt replays the same poisoned history.

This reproduced twice independently on different task content, plus a third time as `hermes kanban decompose`'s "malformed JSON" error (same underlying 400, just misreported by the decompose caller).

## Evidence

Captured via `profiles/<name>/sessions/request_dump_<session>_<ts>.json` (dumped automatically on `non_retryable_client_error`).

- `reason: "non_retryable_client_error"`
- `error.body.message: "No user query found in messages."`
- `request.body.messages`: 25 entries, **role histogram: 1× system, 12× assistant, 12× tool — 0× user**.
- Immediately preceded in `agent.log` by:
  ```
  ... agent.conversation_compression: context compression done: session=<id> messages=26->24 ...
  ... agent.chat_completion_helpers: Streaming failed before delivery: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'No user query found in messages.', ...}}
  ```
  i.e. the very next request after a *successful* compression pass is the one that fails — this is not the separate, already-known timeout/context-ballooning failure mode.

## Suspected contributing factor

Kanban workers are seeded with a deliberately minimal prompt (`gateway/kanban_watchers.py` → `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py::_default_spawn`, `prompt = f"work kanban task {task.id}"`). The real task body is fetched via a tool call afterward, not embedded in the user turn. That means the *only* user-role message in the whole session is short and appears very early. If `_find_last_user_message_idx`'s search window (bounded by `head_end`) or the head/tail boundary computation doesn't line up with where that single early user message actually lives, the tail-anchoring guard can end up with nothing to anchor on for that message once real compression pressure builds up from many tool-call turns — even though the guard's own docstring says this exact scenario (#10896) is what it exists to prevent.

I have not fully root-caused *why* the guard misses this specific case (would need live instrumentation inside a real kanban worker run, which I didn't want to do without confirming with maintainers first) — flagging the mechanism and the reproducible symptom rather than claiming the exact line-level defect.

## Impact

Any `hermes kanban` worker task whose conversation grows long enough to trigger auto-compression (default `threshold_percent=0.50`) is at risk of a hard, non-retryable crash it cannot self-heal from — task-level `max-retries` gets burned uselessly since every retry resumes the same already-poisoned session and fails on the very first subsequent request.

## Environment

- hermes-agent commit: `528159f7aa6a0c234c61685f552cb45f22849c52` (2026-07-03)
- Backend: custom OpenAI-compatible provider (vLLM, Qwen3.6-27B), `context_length=65536`
- Trigger: `hermes kanban dispatch` on a `dev`-profile task with no special config beyond a raised `auxiliary.compression.timeout` (600s, unrelated fix for a different issue)

## Suggested directions (not prescriptive)

1. Add a regression test seeding a kanban-style conversation (single short early user message + many assistant/tool turns) through `context_compressor.compress()` and assert the output always contains ≥1 user-role message.
2. As a defense in depth independent of the compressor: if a provider ever rejects a request with "no user message" style errors, synthesize a minimal placeholder user turn (e.g. `"Continue."`) and retry once, rather than treating it as non-retryable.

items.body:
### Bug: Empty tool_calls array after repair_message_sequence — DeepSeek v4 Flash HTTP 400

This is a follow-up to the previously closed issue #56980 (closed as `not_planned` by maintainer). The same underlying bug persists and has been reproduced again on 2026-07-05 with a new error variant.

### DeepSeek Error Response

> **Error code: 400**
> `Invalid 'messages[569].tool_calls': empty array. Expected an array with minimum length 1, but got an empty array instead.`

Previously the error was `"insufficient tool messages following tool_calls"` (see #56980) — now it is about an **empty `tool_calls` array `[]`**. Both stem from the same root cause.

### Log Evidence (`~/.hermes/logs/agent.log`, session `c3a077993596`, 2026-07-05)

The agent's `repair_message_sequence` runs before every request:

```
2026-07-05 17:14:36,186 INFO [c3a077993596] agent.conversation_loop: Repaired 1 message-alternation violations before request (session=c3a077993596)
```

But immediately after repair, DeepSeek rejects:

```
2026-07-05 17:14:38,134 INFO agent.chat_completion_helpers: Streaming failed before delivery: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': "Invalid 'messages[569].tool_calls': empty array. Expected an array with minimum length 1, but got an empty array instead.", 'type': 'invalid_request_error', 'param': None, 'code': 'invalid_request_error'}}
2026-07-05 17:14:38,136 WARNING [c3a077993596] agent.conversation_loop: API call failed (attempt 1/3) error_type=BadRequestError ...
2026-07-05 17:14:38,361 ERROR [c3a077993596] agent.conversation_loop: Non-retryable client error: Error code: 400 - ...
```

### Session Characteristics

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Session ID | `c3a077993596` |
| Provider | DeepSeek v4 Flash |
| History size | ~571 messages |
| Tool turns | ~219 |
| Triggering action | Simple user query after `bg-review` turn |
| Occurrences | 6 consecutive 400 errors (17:14:38 through 17:20:30) |

### Root Cause (still not fixed)

`repair_message_sequence()` in `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py` does not properly handle the case where an `assistant` message has `tool_calls: []` (empty array). The repair may merge or reorder messages in a way that creates an assistant message with an empty tool_calls array, which DeepSeek's API validation rejects.

### Recovery

Once the first 400 occurs, the session is **permanently stuck** — every retry returns the same 400. The only workaround is starting a new session.

### See Also

- Original report: #56980 (closed `not_planned` without resolution)
- @kshitijk4poor's analysis at https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/56980#issuecomment-2752043164
- Request dumps from session `8a511cac6545` were previously posted on #56980

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Bug Description

`hermes doctor` reports:

```text
model.provider 'moa' is not a recognised provider
```

and suggests the fix:

```text
Run 'hermes config set model.provider <valid_provider>'
```

However, `moa` is a legitimate internal Mixture-of-Agents (MoA) provider used by Hermes itself for Diagnosis presets and multi-model aggregation. It is not a bug in the user's configuration; it is a difference between the provider validation list and the list of actually supported internal providers.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Hermes to use a MoA/Diagnosis preset that sets `model.provider` to `moa`.
2. Run `hermes doctor`.

## Expected Behavior

`hermes doctor` should either:

- Recognise `moa` as a valid internal provider (not just external/commercial ones), or
- If `moa` is intentionally outside the validator, downgrade the message to an informational warning such as:


items.title: cua-driver refresh in `hermes update` can wedge permanently: 300s timeout vs installer's 600s stale-lock window + orphaned lock on timeout

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Summary

`hermes update`'s cua-driver refresh (and `hermes computer-use install --upgrade`) can time out on every run and never recover. Reported by a community user (Windows/via X): "Unable to upgrade CUA using the Hermes update command; it always times out."

## Root cause (two compounding problems)

`_run_cua_driver_installer()` in `hermes_cli/tools_config.py` runs the upstream `curl … install.sh | bash` with `subprocess.run(..., shell=True, timeout=300)`.

**1. Timeout kills the shell, not the installer — orphaning the install lock.**
On `TimeoutExpired`, `subprocess.run` kills only the direct child. The `curl | bash` pipeline / exec'd `_install-rust.sh` grandchildren can survive, and the installer's concurrent-install lock (`~/.cua-driver/packages/.install.lock.d`, pid stamped in `info`) can be left held or stale.

**2. Our 300s timeout is shorter than the installer's own 600s stale-lock recovery window.**
Upstream `_install-rust.sh` waits up to `LOCK_STALE_AFTER_SECONDS=600` before probing the holder pid and force-releasing a stale lock. With our 300s ceiling, a wedged/stale lock means every subsequent `hermes update`:
- hits the lock,
- polls for up to 600s waiting on stale-lock recovery,
- gets killed by our 300s timeout before recovery can ever fire.

Result: **permanently wedged — "always times out"** — with an unactionable message ("timed out. Re-run manually.") that doesn't mention the lock.

A slow GitHub path (throttled regions; the installer fetches 2 raw scripts + a ~15MB tarball with no `--max-time`) can seed the first timeout, after which problem 1+2 make it permanent.

## Expected behavior

- A timed-out install must not leave orphaned installer processes or a held lock.
- A stale lock from a dead holder should be detected and cleared before invoking the installer.
- The timeout should exceed the installer's own 600s stale-lock window.
- The timeout message should name the lock path so users have a manual escape hatch.

## Environment

- Any POSIX platform (lock logic is in the bash installer); reporter is on Windows where the slow-network path also applies.
- `hermes update` with cua-driver on PATH, or `hermes computer-use install --upgrade`.

Related-but-distinct: #47865 (noisy refresh on non-admin macOS — precondition skip, not a hang), #57025 (runtime MCP session-ready timeout, not the installer).
