labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Description

The Desktop app shows "更新未完成 / 后端更新失败" (Backend update failed) modal **every time an update succeeds**, even though the code is actually current. The issue is reproducible and appears in ~15 out of ~30 update sessions in the logs.

## Root Cause

The gateway restart after a successful update triggers the Desktop to re-check for updates, which starts a second `hermes update`. That second run finds no new commits and takes the **"Already up to date" early-return path** (`main.py:9694`), which:

1. Prints `"✓ Already up to date!"` — but **not** `"✓ Update complete!"`
2. Does **not** trigger a gateway restart
3. Returns exit code 0

The Desktop's `applyBackendUpdate()` in `updates.ts:540` sees `exit_code === 0` and calls `finishBackendApply(waitForBackendReturn())`. Since no gateway restart happened, `waitForBackendReturn()` polls `checkHermesUpdate()` and either times out or hits a transient connection drop from the *previous* gateway restart, returning `false` → the error modal appears.

## Reproduction

1. Have an update available (1+ commits behind origin/main)
2. Click update in Desktop → succeeds, gateway restarts
3. ~3 minutes later, Desktop auto-triggers a second update
4. Second update: `git fetch` → "Already up to date!" → exit 0
5. Desktop shows "Backend update failed"

## Log Evidence

```
=== hermes update started 2026-07-05T14:45:22 ===   ← first update, succeeds
✓ Update complete!
  ✓ Restarted hermes-gateway

=== hermes update started 2026-07-05T14:48:39 ===   ← second update (3 min later)
⚕ Updating Hermes Agent...
→ Fetching updates...
✓ Already up to date!
                                                         ← no "Update complete!", no exit status
```

This pattern repeats across 15 update sessions with no outcome recorded.

## Suggested Fix

Either:

**A)** In `_cmd_update_impl`, print `"✓ Update complete!"` before returning on the "Already up to date" path (line ~9694), so the Desktop's action status polling sees a terminal message.

**B)** Have the Desktop skip triggering `applyBackendUpdate()` when `checkBackendUpdates()` finds the backend is already at the latest version (i.e. don't re-run `hermes update` if the backend just restarted and is already current).

**C)** In `finishBackendApply`, if `waitForBackendReturn()` fails, do a secondary check: if `git rev-list HEAD..origin/main --count` is 0, treat it as success rather than error.

Option B is the cleanest — it prevents the unnecessary second update entirely.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent on Linux (server) + Desktop on Windows (ThinkPad P14)
- Update via gateway mode
- `updates.non_interactive_local_changes: stash` (default)

items.title: Config writes can overwrite an unreadable existing config.yaml

labels.name: comp/cli

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Summary

Several `config.yaml` update paths treat an unreadable existing config as an empty config and can then atomically replace the file with only defaults or the newly edited section.

## Affected behavior

If `~/.hermes/config.yaml` exists but cannot be read because of filesystem permissions, transient I/O failure, or a broken mount, `read_raw_config()` returns `{}`. Callers that immediately write the resulting config can lose the user's existing provider, fallback, platform, and tool settings.

Affected paths include:

- `save_config()`
- `hermes config set ...`
- auth login/logout provider updates that write `model.provider`

## Expected behavior

Hermes should fail closed when an existing `config.yaml` cannot be read before a full-file replacement. New config creation should still work when the file does not exist.

## Proof

On current `main`, `read_raw_config()` catches `OSError`/read failures and returns `{}`. The write paths then call `atomic_yaml_write()` with the partial or default config, replacing `config.yaml`.

A regression test can simulate `PermissionError` while reading an existing `config.yaml` and verify that `save_config()` and `config set` refuse to overwrite it and leave the original bytes intact.

## Duplicate check

Searched existing Hermes issues and PRs for:

- `config unreadable overwrite save_config read_raw_config`
- `PermissionError config.yaml save_config`
- `unreadable config.yaml overwrite`

No matching issue or PR was found.

items.title: bug(telegram): fallback-IP transport bypasses #31599 keepalive fix → general-pool CLOSE_WAIT fd leak

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Problem

The keepalive fix for #31599 (`platform_httpx_limits()` wired into the Telegram `HTTPXRequest`) does **not** protect the **fallback-IP transport** path. On a host where `api.telegram.org` is only reachable via `TelegramFallbackTransport` (no proxy, fallback IPs active), the general-request pool still accumulates half-closed (`CLOSE_WAIT`) sockets until the process hits the macOS default `maxfiles=256` and wedges — same failure mode as #31599, different branch.

Observed on a long-lived gateway (10 days, no restart), `hermes` HEAD around v2026.6.19:

```
pid <main>  (ai.hermes.gateway):        289 open fds — 224 CLOSE_WAIT to sticky fallback IP :443
pid <macro> (ai.hermes.gateway-macro):  289 open fds — 227 CLOSE_WAIT
```

Once over 256: `sqlite3.OperationalError: unable to open database file` (kanban dispatcher), `channel_directory: failed to write [Errno 24]`, and user-visibly the Telegram bot hangs forever ("receiving stream response") because no new send/stream socket can be opened:

```
ERROR gateway.platforms.base: [Telegram] Error handling message: [Errno 24] Too many open files: '.../sessions/.sessions_*.tmp'
WARNING telegram_network: [Telegram] Fallback IP 149.154.166.110 failed: All connection attempts failed
```

## Root cause

The fix injects the tuned limits via `httpx_kwargs["limits"]`, but the fallback branch **also** supplies a custom `transport`:

```python
# plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py  (fallback branch)
request = HTTPXRequest(
    **request_kwargs,
    httpx_kwargs=_with_limits({"transport": TelegramFallbackTransport(fallback_ips)}),
)
```

**httpx ignores the client-level `limits` argument whenever a custom `transport` is passed** — `limits` only configures the default transport httpx would otherwise build. So the inner transports in `TelegramFallbackTransport.__init__` run with httpx defaults (`keepalive_expiry=5.0`), and their peer-FIN'd keepalive connections are never reaped before the fd limit is hit. The polling pool is periodically reset by `_drain_polling_connections()`, but the general-request pool (heavy `editMessageText` during streaming) is not.

The proxy branch (`elif proxy_url:`) is unaffected because it passes `proxy=` (no custom transport), so `_with_limits()` there does apply — which is why #31599 looked fixed.

## Proposed fix

Pass the tuned `limits` **into** `TelegramFallbackTransport` (forwarded to its inner `AsyncHTTPTransport`s) instead of onto the client where httpx discards it. Small change, no effect on the proxy / direct-DNS branches. PR to follow.

## Workaround

Raise the launchd `NumberOfFiles` limit (tracked separately in #36899) and/or restart the affected gateway on an fd-count threshold. These defer but don't fix the leak.

Related: #31599 (parent, proxy variant), #30230 (fd-limit symptom), #36899 (plist NumberOfFiles).

```
    ls = p.start_login(redirect_uri=_redirect_uri(request))
File "/opt/hermes/plugins/dashboard_auth/basic/__init__.py", line 230, in start_login
    raise NotImplementedError(
```

## Summary

Gateway process memory grows from ~300 MB (fresh start) to **1.4–1.6 GB** over approximately 20 hours of uptime on a lightly-loaded Debian 13 instance (Hetzner CX53, single Telegram DM channel, one daily cron job). The daily cron-triggered planned-restart incidentally keeps it in check, which means the leak presents as routine recycling rather than a crash — making it easy to miss entirely.

Related to / additional evidence for: #48287

## Environment

- **Hermes Agent**: v0.18.0 (2026.7.1) · upstream dec4485d
- **OS**: Debian 13 (trixie), kernel 6.12.88+deb13-cloud-amd64 (Hetzner CX53 VPS)
- **Python**: 3.11.15
- **Gateway mode**: systemd user unit, single Telegram DM channel
- **Load**: Very light — one user, one daily digest cron job

## Observed memory at each planned-restart (systemd journal)

| Date | Approx uptime | RSS at stop |
|------|--------------|-------------|
| Jul 3 11:33 | ~53 min (fresh) | 336 MB |
| Jul 4 08:04 | ~20.5 h | **1.6 GB** (~5× growth) |
| Jul 5 08:03 | ~20 h | **1.4 GB** (~4.5× growth) |
| Jul 5 08:03+ | ~2.9 h at time of writing | 315 MB (fresh) |

```
Jul 03 11:33:22 hermes-gateway.service: Consumed 53min 9.625s CPU time, 336M memory peak.
Jul 04 08:04:47 hermes-gateway.service: Consumed 3min 50.212s CPU time, 1.6G memory peak.
Jul 05 08:03:33 hermes-gateway.service: Consumed 3min 31.782s CPU time, 1.4G memory peak.
```

A daily digest cron fires at 08:00. Hermes schedules a planned-restart watcher tied to the cron runner PID; when that PID exits (~3–4 min later), the gateway recycles. - No MCP servers running (rules out #42073 Playwright leak vector)
- No dashboard process running
- The planned-restart mechanism functioning as a de-facto memory safety valve while the underlying leak remains unaddressed feels like a design concern worth surfacing — a busier or less-scheduled instance would not benefit from this accidental mitigation

items.title: [Bug]: Planned-restart fires while cron delivery is in-flight — message silently dropped

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Summary

When a cron job completes and triggers a planned-restart of the gateway, the gateway stops *while* it is in the process of delivering the cron output. The delivery is lost with no error, no retry, and no indication to the user that it was dropped.

## How the planned-restart mechanism works

When Hermes spawns a cron agent, it registers a watcher service tied to the cron runner PID. The watcher fires the moment that PID exits. If the cron runner exits while the gateway is still sending the delivery to Telegram (or any platform), the gateway stops mid-send and the delivery is silently gone.

## Observed timeline (two consecutive mornings)

```
Jul 04 08:00 — morning digest cron fires
Jul 04 08:01:32 — planned-restart watcher registered (cron PID exits after LLM call completes)
Jul 04 08:04:47 — gateway stopped (delivery window: 08:01-08:04 — silent)
Jul 04 08:04:47 — gateway back up

Jul 05 08:00 — same cron fires
Jul 05 08:00:22 — planned-restart watcher registered
Jul 05 08:03:33 — gateway stopped
Jul 05 08:03:33 — gateway back up
```

Both mornings: cron completed, gateway recycled, delivery never arrived. The output file on disk shows a fully-written response. The message was never sent to the user.

## Root cause

The planned-restart fires on cron-PID-exit, not on delivery-complete. There is a structural gap between "cron agent finished generating output" and "gateway finished delivering that output to the platform." For Telegram (network round-trip, potential reconnect after a Bad Gateway event the night before) this window is real and reproducible.

## Why rescheduling the cron is not a fix

Shifting the cron to a different time is a sticking plaster. The race condition exists regardless of schedule: any cron that causes a planned-restart will have this delivery gap. A busier instance with multiple cron jobs would hit this more frequently.

## Proposed fix directions

1. **Delay the planned-restart until the delivery queue is drained** — the watcher should wait for an idle or delivery-complete signal rather than firing immediately on cron-PID-exit.
2. **Durable delivery queue** — write the pending delivery to disk before the cron PID exits; replay on next gateway start.
3. **Synchronous delivery before cron-PID exit** — confirm delivery before the cron runner process exits, so the watcher cannot fire while a delivery is in flight.

## Environment

- **Hermes Agent**: v0.18.0 (2026.7.1) upstream dec4485d
- **OS**: Debian 13 (trixie), systemd user session
- **Platform**: Telegram
- **Cron**: one daily digest job, deliver=telegram

The Desktop MOA settings panel calls `PUT /api/model/moa` to save preset changes. The endpoint's Pydantic payload model `MoaConfigPayload` does not declare `save_traces` or `trace_dir` as fields, and `set_moa_models` does a wholesale overwrite of `cfg["moa"]`. As a result, any `save_traces: true` (and `trace_dir`) value I have set by hand-editing `~/.hermes/config.yaml` is silently dropped every time I save anything through the Desktop MOA GUI — without warning, and without any log entry.

This effectively prevents enabling MOA trace persistence through the Desktop UI, and silently disables it for users who already have it working via hand-edited yaml.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Hand-edit ~/.hermes/config.yaml, add under the moa: block:

   save_traces: true
   trace_dir: ""

2. Run a MOA session from Desktop. Verify: a trace JSONL file appears at ~/.hermes/moa-traces/<session_id>.jsonl.

3. Open Desktop -> Settings -> Model -> Mixture of Agents panel.

4. Change any preset parameter (e.g. add a reference model, change max_tokens).

5. Click Save.

6. Re-open ~/.hermes/config.yaml: the save_traces: true line is gone. save_traces and trace_dir are dropped from yaml.

Expected: the two hand-set fields are preserved across saves.
Actual: both fields silently disappear.


### Expected Behavior

After saving through the Desktop MOA panel, manually-configured save_traces and trace_dir values remain intact in ~/.hermes/config.yaml. Subsequent MOA runs continue to produce JSONL trace files.

### Actual Behavior

After saving through the Desktop MOA panel, save_traces and trace_dir are silently removed from cfg["moa"] in ~/.hermes/config.yaml. Subsequent MOA runs produce NO trace file under ~/.hermes/moa-traces/, with no warning to the user.

To restore trace persistence, the user must hand-edit yaml again - and the same loss recurs on the next save.

Configuration (config.yaml, .env, hermes setup)

N/A (CLI only)

```shell

[output saved locally at /tmp/hermes_debug_report.txt - 10032 lines]
```

items.title: [Bug]: Piper TTS writes raw WAV to .ogg output path — Opus conversion skipped, Telegram shows 0-second voice bubble

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
**Version:** v0.17.x (confirmed on current latest image)

**What happened**

When using Piper as the TTS provider with `voice_only` mode on Telegram,
voice replies arrive as a 0-second voice bubble. The file is delivered as
a voice note (correct format, correct size — e.g. 186 KB for a ~10s reply),
but Telegram cannot read the duration and shows 0:00.

**Root cause**

`_generate_piper_tts` always writes raw WAV bytes to `output_path`,
regardless of its extension (the docstring says: "Caller handles downstream
conversion"). When called from `_send_voice_reply` in `gateway/run.py`,
the caller passes a `.ogg` path. The conversion logic afterwards checks:

    elif (
        want_opus
        and provider in {"edge", "neutts", "minimax", "xai", "kittentts", "piper"}
        and not file_str.endswith(".ogg")
    ):

Since `file_str` already ends with `.ogg`, this branch is skipped — the
code assumes the file is already Opus. It is not: it contains raw WAV bytes
in a `.ogg` container. Telegram accepts it but cannot derive a duration.

**This is distinct from #57049**, which affects the `voice.auto_tts` path
in `gateway/platforms/base.py` (filename pattern: `tts_<timestamp>.mp3`).
This bug affects `_send_voice_reply` in `gateway/run.py` (filename pattern:
`tts_reply_<uuid>.ogg`) — the path that #57049 itself cites as "already
working correctly".

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Configure `tts.provider: piper` with an absolute `.onnx` voice path.
2. Set `voice_only` mode on Telegram.
3. Send a voice message and observe the reply.

**Expected:** Voice bubble with correct duration.
**Actual:** Voice bubble shows 0:00.

**Proposed fix**

Insert a Piper-specific case before the existing `elif` to rename the file
to `.wav` first, then convert:

    elif want_opus and provider == "piper" and file_str.endswith(".ogg"):
        wav_path = file_str[:-4] + ".wav"
        os.rename(file_str, wav_path)
        opus_path = _convert_to_opus(wav_path)
        if opus_path:
            file_str = opus_path
            voice_compatible = True

Verified working on two live deployments (2026-07-05).
Happy to open a PR if welcome.

items.body:
## Bug Description

After updating Hermes Agent (config_version 32 → 33), all configured stdio MCP servers are eagerly started at agent boot instead of lazily on first use. Previously, servers were only started when their tools were first called.

The MCP configuration itself hasn't changed — only the lifecycle behavior.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure multiple stdio MCP servers (npx/uvx-based) in config.yaml
2. Start Hermes Agent
3. All MCP servers spawn immediately at boot
4. Each server starts multiple times — observed hermes-studio started 5 times in 7 seconds
5. Duplicate instances accumulate over time without cleanup

## Actual Behavior

- Each MCP server instance consumes 60-100 MB of memory
- With 10+ configured servers, 800+ MB baseline memory usage
- Multiple duplicate instances per server accumulate
- Processes are never cleaned up when sessions end

Log from `mcp-stderr.log` showing repeated starts:
```
[2026-07-05 20:07:04] starting MCP server 'hermes-studio'
[2026-07-05 20:07:04] starting MCP server 'hermes-studio'
[2026-07-05 20:07:05] starting MCP server 'hermes-studio'
[2026-07-05 20:07:07] starting MCP server 'hermes-studio'
[2026-07-05 20:07:11] starting MCP server 'hermes-studio'
```

Server process management (from mcp-stderr.log): `modes/mcpserver.go:276` / `modes/mcpserver.go:305`

## Expected Behavior

1. Lazy loading: MCP servers should start only when a tool from that server is first called
2. Singleton instances: reuse existing process instead of spawning duplicates
3. Cleanup: idle MCP processes should be terminated when no longer needed
4. Config option for lifecycle policy (eager/lazy)

## Environment

- Windows 10
- Hermes Agent, config_version 33
- 15.7 GB RAM
- ~12 configured MCP servers (mix of npx and HTTP transports)

## Workaround

Setting `enabled: false` on infrequently used MCP servers prevents them from starting at boot, but the old lazy-loading behavior cannot be restored through configuration.

items.title: [Bug]: Gateway tool dispatch returns fewer skills than fresh subprocess — _find_all_skills result diverges between long-running gateway and new Python process

items.body:
# [Bug]: Gateway tool dispatch returns fewer skills than fresh subprocess — `_find_all_skills` result diverges between long-running gateway and new Python process

## Bug Description

The `skills_list` and `skill_view` tools in the live gateway process return a **subset** of skills compared to calling the same `_find_all_skills()` function from a fresh Python subprocess. The gateway consistently returns 80 skills while a fresh subprocess returns 88. The missing 8 skills span entire categories that are invisible to the agent at runtime.

This means the agent **cannot discover or load** skills in these categories through normal tool calls, even though the files are valid, parseable, and on disk.

## Missing categories (8 total)

- `meta` (review-updates, save)
- `hermes-config` (model-picker-editing)
- `content-creation` (daily-learning-drip)
- `scheduled` (briefing, clickup-token-health, langfuse-pipeline-monitor, trace-discovery)
- `thinking` (council)
- `tools` (browser-automation)
- `transfer` (external-delivery)
- `video` (kie-video-creator)

## Steps to Reproduce

**Environment:**
- Hermes v0.18.0, upstream HEAD `7e8f50a14` + local overlay `f78472ec`
- Profile: `merlin`
- `HERMES_HOME=/home/bigbox/.hermes/profiles/merlin`
- `SKILLS_DIR=/home/bigbox/.hermes/profiles/merlin/skills`
- Linux (Pop!_OS 24.04), Python 3.12

**Step 1 — Verify skills exist on disk:**
```bash
ls ~/.hermes/profiles/merlin/skills/meta/review-updates/SKILL.md
# File exists, readable, valid frontmatter
```

**Step 2 — Fresh subprocess returns correct count (88):**
```python
# Run in a fresh Python process (e.g., via terminal tool)
cd ~/.hermes/hermes-agent && python3 -c "
from tools.skills_tool import _find_all_skills, skills_list
import json

all_skills = _find_all_skills()
print(f'_find_all_skills: {len(all_skills)} skills')

meta = [s for s in all_skills if s.get('category') == 'meta']
print(f'Meta skills: {[s[\"name\"] for s in meta]}')

result = json.loads(skills_list())
print(f'skills_list tool: {result[\"count\"]} skills')
"
```

Expected output:
```
_find_all_skills: 88 skills
Meta skills: ['review-updates', 'save']
skills_list tool: 88 skills
```

**Step 3 — Live gateway tool returns fewer (80):**
```
# In the running TUI session:
skills_list → returns 80 skills, count: 80
# Missing categories: meta, hermes-config, content-creation, scheduled, thinking, tools, transfer, video
```

**Step 4 — `skill_view` fails for missing skills:**
```
skill_view("review-updates")
→ {"success": false, "error": "Skill 'review-updates' not found."}
```

**Step 5 — `skill_view` works from subprocess:**
```bash
cd ~/.hermes/hermes-agent && python3 -c "
from tools.skills_tool import skill_view
import json
result = json.loads(skill_view('review-updates'))
print(result['success'])  # True
"
```

## Root cause hypothesis

The gateway process (long-running, started via systemd) has a **stale or divergent skill index** compared to a fresh Python process. Possible causes:

1. **Module-level caching at import time** — some module initialization captures a skill list that doesn't refresh
2. **`os.walk` / `rglob` behavior difference** — the gateway's process context (working directory, environment, or import state) causes `iter_skill_index_files` or `_find_all_skills` to skip certain directories
3. **`_EXCLUDED_SKILL_DIRS` divergence** — the excluded dirs set is identical when tested, but there may be a runtime state difference
4. **Tool dispatch uses a different code path** — the tool handler might not call `_find_all_skills()` directly

## What I've verified

- `SKILLS_DIR` resolves to `/home/bigbox/.hermes/profiles/merlin/skills` in both contexts ✅
- `HERMES_HOME` is correctly set in both contexts ✅
- `_EXCLUDED_SKILL_DIRS` is identical (`.mypy_cache`, `.venv`, `venv`, `.git`, `.archive`, `__pycache__`, etc.) ✅
- `_skill_lookup_path_error('review-updates')` returns `None` (no path validation issue) ✅
- Gateway restart does **not** fix the issue ✅
- `skill_view('review-updates')` succeeds from a fresh Python subprocess with identical env ✅
- The `.skills_prompt_snapshot.json` includes the missing skills ✅
- `get_skill_commands()` (agent/skill_commands.py) returns all 88 skills including missing ones ✅

## Impact

- Agent cannot discover or load 8 skills (spanning 8 categories) through normal `skills_list` / `skill_view` tool calls
- These skills are still usable via `read_file` workarounds but the agent must know to bypass the tool
- The system prompt's `available_skills` list (injected at session start) **does** include the missing skills, so the model knows they exist — but the tool layer can't load them, creating a confusing contradiction

## Environment

- Hermes version: v0.18.0 (upstream `7e8f50a14` + local overlay `f78472ec`)
- OS: Pop!_OS 24.04 (Ubuntu-based), kernel 6.17.0
- Python: 3.12
- Profile: merlin (multi-profile setup: merlin, doc, hermes-cs, hermes-wb, picasso, collector)
- Gateway: systemd user unit `hermes-gateway-merlin.service`

items.title: 500 Internal Server Error when BasicAuthProvider is the only auth provider (auto-SSO crashes on password-only provider)

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: comp/dashboard
labels.description: Web dashboard / control panel UI (dashboard/, landing)

items.body:
## Description

**500 Internal Server Error** when opening the dashboard URL (e.g. `https://hermes.upsay.com.br/`) if **BasicAuthProvider** (password-only) is the only registered auth provider.

## Repro Steps

1. Configure Hermes dashboard with **BasicAuthProvider** as the only auth provider (a password-only provider, bundled with Hermes core)
2. Open `https://<dashboard-url>/` while **not authenticated**
3. Dashboard returns **HTTP 500**

## Root Cause

The `_auto_sso_response()` function in `hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/middleware.py` (line ~185) implements an auto-SSO optimization: when exactly **one** interactive provider is registered, it auto-redirects to `/auth/login?provider=<name>` to skip the login-page interstitial.

However, `BasicAuthProvider` is a **password-only** provider — it sets `supports_password = True` and does **not** implement `start_login()` (raises `NotImplementedError`). The `/auth/login` route unconditionally calls `p.start_login(redirect_uri=...)`, which crashes with:

```
NotImplementedError: BasicAuthProvider is password-only; there is no OAuth redirect
flow. The login page POSTs to /auth/password-login instead.
```

The `_auto_sso_response` function has **no guard** checking whether the provider actually supports the OAuth redirect flow before redirecting.

## Proposed Fix

In `_auto_sso_response()`, after selecting the single provider, skip the auto-SSO redirect if the provider has `supports_password=True`. The `/login` page already renders a credential form for password providers, so there's no interstitial to skip:

```python
    provider = providers[0]

    # Password-only providers (e.g. BasicAuth) have no OAuth redirect flow;
    # their login page renders a credential form that POSTs to
    # /auth/password-login. Auto-redirecting to /auth/login would call
    # start_login() which raises NotImplementedError — crash, 500.
    # Fall through to /login so the user sees the credential form.
    if getattr(provider, "supports_password", False):
        return None

    from hermes_cli.dashboard_auth.prefix import prefix_from_request
    prefix = prefix_from_request(request)
    ...
```

## Affected File

`hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/middleware.py` — `_auto_sso_response()` function

## Tests

All 77 relevant tests pass:

```
tests/hermes_cli/test_dashboard_auth_middleware.py  — 33 passed
tests/hermes_cli/test_dashboard_auth_401_reauth.py  — 44 passed
```

## Additional Context

- The `list_session_providers()` already filters on `supports_session=True`, so token-only providers are correctly excluded from the auto-SSO check.
- A provider that supports **both** password and OAuth (currently hypothetical) would also be skipped by this guard — acceptable because the login page would show both options anyway.

items.title: Feature request: make CLI voice mode use generic TTSProvider.stream()

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: area/streaming
labels.description: Streaming responses: gateway delivery, provider wire

items.body:
## Summary

Hermes already exposes a generic `TTSProvider.stream()` interface, but the local CLI realtime voice mode currently appears to use a provider-specific streaming path instead of the active TTS provider abstraction. In practice this means a plugin provider can implement `stream()` and still not be usable by CLI voice mode without Hermes core changes.

## Current behavior

From local inspection of the Windows Hermes Agent install:

- `agent/tts_provider.py` defines optional `TTSProvider.stream()`.
- `tools/tts_tool.py` dispatches file-based synthesis to plugin providers selected by `tts.provider`.
- Gateway/platform paths, including Discord voice channel playback, use file-based `text_to_speech_tool(...)` output and already work with plugin TTS providers.
- CLI voice mode has a realtime streaming path that is currently tied to ElevenLabs instead of the generic provider registry.

## Why this matters

MiniMax supports both normal TTS and streaming TTS:

- Plain TTS docs: https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/speech-t2a-intro
- WebSocket streaming TTS docs: https://platform.minimax.io/docs/guides/speech-t2a-websocket

A standalone MiniMax plugin can already support normal Hermes TTS through `synthesize()`, and can expose a `stream()` method backed by MiniMax WebSocket events (`task_start`, `task_continue`, `task_finish`) that yield audio chunks from `data.audio`.

However, without a generic CLI voice-mode integration, that provider-level `stream()` method is effectively unused by local CLI voice mode.

## Proposal

Please make CLI voice mode use the active TTS provider abstraction for realtime playback:

1. Resolve the active provider through the TTS registry/config path used by `text_to_speech_tool`.
2. If the provider implements `stream()`, use a generic streaming playback path.
3. Keep the existing ElevenLabs behavior by adapting it into the same provider-level path or by preserving it as a fallback.
4. Fall back to file-based synthesis when the provider does not implement streaming.
5. Standardize the stream contract enough for playback code to know what it is receiving.

The last point probably needs an explicit format contract. Today `stream()` returns `Iterator[bytes]`, but local speaker playback needs to know whether chunks are encoded MP3/Opus/PCM, plus sample rate/channel metadata for PCM. Two possible approaches:

- Add provider metadata methods/properties for stream format, sample rate, and channel count.
- Or introduce a small `AudioChunk`/`AudioStreamInfo` style object instead of raw bytes only.

## Acceptance criteria

- A plugin TTS provider selected via `tts.provider` can power CLI voice mode if it implements `stream()`.
- Providers without streaming still work through the existing synthesize-to-file path.
- Existing ElevenLabs CLI streaming behavior remains functional.
- Interrupt/cleanup handling closes the provider stream and audio output cleanly.
- Tests cover plugin stream provider selection, fallback to file synthesis, and the ElevenLabs compatibility path.

## Related external plugin work

A MiniMax plugin repo was created to validate this externally without modifying Hermes core:

https://github.com/Josephur/hermes-minimax-plugins

The `tts` plugin uses provider name `minimax-tts` because Hermes reserves the built-in provider name `minimax`.

items.title: [Bug]: resume_pending_expired silently creates new session without notifying user or properly closing the old one

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug Description

When a gateway session has `resume_pending=True` (set after a drain-timeout restart) and API recovery fails (e.g. large context causes repeated timeouts), the `resume_pending` marker is never cleared. After `gateway_auto_continue_freshness` seconds (default 3600s), the next inbound message silently triggers a `resume_pending_expired` auto-reset:

1. A **brand-new session is created** with `history=0`, discarding the routing to the active conversation
2. The user **receives no notification** that their session was replaced
3. The old session is ended with the generic `end_reason="session_reset"` in state.db — indistinguishable from a normal idle/daily reset
4. The agent receives a **misleading system note** ("expired due to inactivity") when the actual cause is restart-recovery timeout

This was triggered in production on two independent gateway profiles simultaneously (dingding and bala), both with `session_reset.mode: none` and large contexts (~370k tokens). The gateway restarted at 17:30, recovery API calls timed out by 17:42, and at ~19:22 (1h52m later) a user message created a new session. The new session's title was auto-generated from the first message ("召唤小可", "可爱的中文打招呼"), making it look like an intentional new conversation.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have an active gateway session with a large context (>100k tokens)
2. Restart the gateway in a way that causes drain timeout (`Skipping .clean_shutdown marker`)
3. The gateway marks the session `resume_pending=True` and attempts auto-resume
4. The auto-resume API call fails (e.g. connection timeout on large context)
5. Wait `gateway_auto_continue_freshness` seconds (default 3600s, configured at `agent.gateway_auto_continue_freshness`)
6. Send any message on the same platform chat

Expected: user receives a notification and is offered `/resume`; OR the freshness window restarts on each failed recovery attempt.

Actual: a new session is created silently; `title_generation` names it after the first message; the old session is closed with `"session_reset"` in the DB.

## Expected Behavior

- The user should receive the same style of notification that `suspended` and `idle`/`daily` resets already send:
  ```
  ◐ Session automatically reset (gateway restart recovery timed out).
  Conversation history cleared.
  Use /resume to browse and restore a previous session.
  ```
- The agent's system context note should accurately say "gateway restart recovery timed out" rather than "expired due to inactivity"
- The old session's `end_reason` in state.db should be `"resume_pending_expired"` (not the generic `"session_reset"`) for auditability

## Actual Behavior

New session created at `history=0`, no user-facing message, agent gets wrong context note, old session ends as `"session_reset"`.

Log evidence (two profiles, same ~19:22 timestamp, ~1h52m after 17:30 restart):

```
# dingding profile
17:30:09 Gateway drain timed out — Skipping .clean_shutdown marker
17:30:52 [57182b] agent_init: attempting auto-resume (history=2126, ~369k tokens)
17:41:06 [57182b] Stream stale for 300s — killing connection
17:42:01 [57182b] API call failed after 3 retries (MiniMax timeout)
# ... 1h40m gap, resume_pending never cleared ...
19:22:32 inbound msg='小可'
19:22:32 [57182b] agent_init (stale, never used)
19:22:32 [3dc5bf3f] conversation turn: history=0   ← brand new session
19:22:36 title_generation → title = "召唤小可"

# bala profile — same pattern, 19:23
19:23:51 [d107459d] conversation turn: history=0
19:23:56 title_generation → title = "可爱的中文打招呼"
```

## Affected Component

- Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)
- Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

## Messaging Platform

- WeChat (iLink/Weixin adapter), but the bug is platform-agnostic

## Debug Report

Reproduction confirmed on two production profiles (dingding, bala) running v0.18.0 on the same host. Logs and state.db analysis available; no `hermes debug share` attached as this contains production data.

## Operating System

Ubuntu 22.04 (Linux 6.8.0-124-generic)

## Python Version

3.11.15

## Hermes Version

v0.18.0 (2026.7.1) · upstream 605727e3

## Root Cause Analysis

**`gateway/session.py` — `get_or_create_session`** (line ~1353–1393):

```python
elif entry.resume_pending:
    reset_reason = self._should_reset(entry, source)
    if not reset_reason:
        _fw = auto_continue_freshness_window()
        _ref_time = entry.last_resume_marked_at or entry.updated_at
        if _fw > 0 and (now - _ref_time).total_seconds() > _fw:
            reset_reason = "resume_pending_expired"   # ← falls into was_auto_reset=True
        else:
            return entry  # normal resume
```

`resume_pending_expired` is treated as an auto-reset exactly like `idle`/`daily`/`suspended`, but:

1. **`gateway/run.py` — `_handle_message_with_agent`** (line ~10279–10336): The `_was_auto_reset` notification block has explicit handling for `"suspended"`, `"daily"`, and a generic `else` that produces the wrong wording. `"resume_pending_expired"` hits the generic `else` with: context note "expired due to inactivity", notification only gated on `policy.notify and had_activity` (so `session_reset.mode: none` users never see it because the policy isn't checked for this path), and `reason_text = f"inactive for {duration}"` (wrong).

2. **DB end_reason**: The old session is always ended with the hardcoded `"session_reset"` string regardless of the actual reset reason (line ~1442), making it impossible to distinguish a `resume_pending_expired` event from a normal idle reset in post-mortem analysis.

## Proposed Fix

Three changes (PR ready):

**1. `gateway/run.py`** — add `resume_pending_expired` as an explicit case:
- Correct system note for the agent: "gateway restart recovery timed out"  
- Always notify the user (like `suspended`), regardless of `policy.notify`
- Correct `reason_text`: "gateway restart recovery timed out"

**2. `gateway/session.py`** — pass `auto_reset_reason` as the `end_reason` to `end_session` instead of always using the hardcoded `"session_reset"`:
```python
_db_end_reason = auto_reset_reason if auto_reset_reason else "session_reset"
self._db.end_session(db_end_session_id, _db_end_reason)
```

**3. Tests** — extend `tests/gateway/test_session_reset_notify.py` with cases covering `resume_pending_expired` notification behavior.

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Root Cause

`gateway/run.py` line 619 defines `_auto_continue_freshness_window()` as a thin lazy-import wrapper:

```python
def _auto_continue_freshness_window() -> float:
    from gateway.session import auto_continue_freshness_window
    return auto_continue_freshness_window()
```

This creates a hidden runtime coupling: if `gateway.session` ever moves, renames, or removes `auto_continue_freshness_window`, the gateway crashes **on every startup** with:

```
ImportError: cannot import name 'auto_continue_freshness_window' from 'gateway.session'
```

The crash occurs inside `_schedule_resume_pending_sessions()`, called from `runner.start()` — the gateway can never finish initialising. systemd restarts it immediately, producing an infinite crash-loop. There is no user-visible warning ahead of the failure.

## How It Was Triggered

A local downstream refactor of `gateway/session.py` (FM9 startup-pruning fix) removed `auto_continue_freshness_window` from `session.py` without updating the import in `run.py`. The gateway entered a restart loop (90+ restarts) before the broken import was identified.

The upstream code does not yet exhibit this crash, but the lazy-import design makes the dependency invisible to linters and static analysis — any future refactor of `gateway.session` can silently reintroduce it.

## Proposed Fix

Inline the three-line env-read logic directly into `_auto_continue_freshness_window()`. The function becomes self-contained and refactor-safe. All existing call sites are unaffected (signature unchanged).

See PR for the two-line diff.

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main

items.body:
The log sequence per turn:
1. Response is streamed via Flushing text batch calls (multiple chunks)
2. By the time the agent finishes generating, content_delivered=True because streaming already pushed the content
3. The "normal final send" is suppressed as a duplicate
4. The macOS client briefly renders the streamed message, then removes it

Not affected
- Messages that complete before streaming threshold (short/fast responses) — these stick normally
- Intermediate/polling messages (like "checking..." or clarifying questions) — these also stick
- Other Telegram clients may or may not exhibit the same issue (only macOS Desktop confirmed)

Likely root cause
The Telegram platform adapter's streaming implementation sends partial content as it's generated, then when the response is fully ready, suppresses the final delivery as a duplicate. The macOS Desktop client appears to interpret the streamed-content-then-suppression cycle as a deletion or replacement, removing the visible message.

Possible fix direction
Ensure the streamed delivery properly finalizes/commits the message on completion rather than suppressing the final send entirely, or send a dedicated "message finalized" signal that tells the client the message is complete and should persist.

Reproduction
1. Ask the agent a question that will produce a long enough response to trigger streaming
2. Observe on Telegram Desktop (macOS) — message appears briefly then disappears
3. Logs confirm streamed=True, content_delivered=True, and the final send being suppressed

Environment
- Platform: Telegram Desktop (macOS)
- Hermes profile: main
- Gateway mode: streaming (default)
- Model: Agent model may vary — symptom is gateway-level, not model-level

## Bug: Sessions permanently stuck in "Stream stale" loop — never recovers

### Description

Once a session encounters a "Stream stale" timeout, **all subsequent retries also stale permanently**. The session enters an infinite loop of: API call → 180s timeout → kill connection → retry → 180s timeout → kill → ... This never recovers, even after days.

### Environment

- **Hermes version:** v0.18.0 (2026.7.1)
- **Python:** 3.11.2
- **OpenAI SDK:** 2.24.0
- **httpx:** 0.28.1
- **OS:** Debian 12 (NAS)
- **Provider:** Xiaomi MiMo (`token-plan-cn.xiaomimimo.com`)

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Start Hermes gateway with Telegram/Feishu platforms
2. Have a conversation that triggers tool calls (terminal, etc.)
3. After some successful API calls, the stream stale detector fires (180s no chunks)
4. From this point, ALL subsequent API calls for this session also stale
5. Session never recovers — even after hours/days of retrying

### Expected Behavior

After a stale timeout:
1. The connection should be killed ✅ (this works)
2. A fresh connection should succeed ✅ (this does NOT work)
3. After N consecutive failures, the session should be reset or the user notified

### Actual Behavior

After a stale timeout:
1. Connection is killed ✅
2. New OpenAI client is created ✅  
3. Next API call is made... but also receives no chunks for 180s ❌
4. This repeats forever (observed: 494 consecutive failures over 3+ days on one session)

### Evidence

**1045 total "Stream stale" warnings across 10+ sessions.** Top affected sessions:

| Session ID | Stale Count | Duration | Model |
|---|---|---|---|
| 20260704_160915_f1d0aa05 | 494 | 3+ days | mimo-v2.5-pro |
| 20260702_222229_726fb44d | 233 | 3+ days | mimo-v2.5 |
| 20260705_170226_0877fba6 | 116 | 6+ hours | mimo-v2.5 |

**Key finding: The API itself is NOT the problem.** Testing from the same NAS:
- `curl` to the same endpoint → responds in <1s ✅
- `httpx.post()` with streaming → works perfectly ✅  
- `openai.OpenAI().chat.completions.create()` with streaming → works perfectly ✅

All tests use the same API key, same endpoint, same machine. Only Hermes's agent loop fails.

### Root Cause Analysis

The issue is in `interruptible_streaming_api_call()` in `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py`.

When the stale detector fires:
1. It kills the connection (`_close_request_client_once("stale_stream_kill")`)
2. It creates a new OpenAI client (`_replace_primary_openai_client`)
3. The retry loop sends the **same request payload** again

But the same payload consistently produces the same stale result. This suggests:
- The API may have an issue with specific message sequences (e.g., certain tool outputs)
- Or the agent's conversation state becomes corrupted in a way that causes the API to hang
- The stale detector correctly identifies the problem but the retry mechanism doesn't break the cycle

### Impact

- **Severe resource waste:** 1045 stale warnings × 180s each = ~52 hours of wasted CPU time
- **User-facing:** Messages sent during stale periods get no response
- **Silent failure:** No notification to the user that the session is stuck

### Suggested Fixes

1. **Add a consecutive failure limit:** After N consecutive stale failures (e.g., 5), give up and notify the user or reset the session
2. **Add user notification:** After the first stale, send a message like "⚠️ API connection issue, retrying..." instead of silent failure
3. **Add exponential backoff:** Instead of retrying every 180s, increase the wait time (180s → 360s → 720s)
4. **Investigate payload-specific hangs:** Add logging of the request payload hash when stale occurs to identify if specific message patterns trigger the issue

### Workaround

Set `HERMES_STREAM_STALE_TIMEOUT=60` in the environment to reduce wait time from 180s to 60s per attempt. This doesn't fix the issue but reduces wasted time.

The dashboard spawns a TUI child whose `HERMES_TUI_GATEWAY_URL` is built in `_build_gateway_ws_url()` (`hermes_cli/web_server.py`) from `app.state.bound_host`. When bound to `0.0.0.0`, the child dials `ws://0.0.0.0:9119/api/ws`.

In setups where a forward proxy (here: Infisical Agent Vault MITM) is configured via `HTTPS_PROXY` with a fixed `NO_PROXY` that does not include `0.0.0.0`, this ws connection is routed through the forward proxy, which cannot dial the wildcard address → `gateway websocket connection failed` / `gateway startup timeout`, and the dashboard chat tab never connects.

## Expected

The in-container ws client should dial a loopback address (`127.0.0.1`) when the bind host is a wildcard (`0.0.0.0` / `::`), since both the dashboard and its TUI child run in the same container. The bind should stay `0.0.0.0` for external reachability; only the client netloc should use loopback.

## Suggested fix

In `_build_gateway_ws_url()` and `_build_sidecar_url()`, substitute:

```python
client_host = "127.0.0.1" if host in ("0.0.0.0", "::") else host
```

for the client netloc, leaving `app.state.bound_host` and the uvicorn bind untouched.

## Workaround currently in use

Local patch doing exactly the above (happy to open a PR).

items.title: [Feature]: Bounded main-agent fallback when the active model hits quota or session limits

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Summary

Closed issue #16525 proposed a broad agent-callable `model_switch` tool and was rejected with "We do not want this".

This request is narrower.

The problem is not general agent autonomy for its own sake. The practical gap is that autonomous Hermes workloads can get stranded when a configured model/provider hits quota or session limits mid-run, and there is no built-in way for the running agent workflow to degrade to a pre-approved cheaper model without human intervention.

## Real-world failure mode

In a multi-profile self-hosted deployment, 4 Hermes profiles shared one Ollama Cloud account and one weekly GPU-time session budget.

A background Honcho deriver workload exhausted the session limit on `gemma4:31b-cloud`. After that, every subsequent API call returned 429 until the session reset. The workflow had no built-in way to detect that quota exhaustion and continue on a lighter pre-approved model. We had to patch health monitoring and build manual alerting around it.

That is manageable for attended chat. It is not manageable for cron jobs, background work, or overnight autonomous processing.

## Request

Add a constrained fallback/escalation mechanism for autonomous runs when the active model becomes unavailable due to quota/session/rate-limit exhaustion.

Examples of acceptable scope:

1. **Job/session-level fallback chain for the main agent**
   - If the active model returns a configured class of failures (`429`, quota exhausted, provider unavailable), Hermes can retry on the next allowed model in a user-defined allowlist.
   - This would be similar in spirit to provider fallback, but for the active agent path, not just auxiliary tasks.

2. **Approval-bounded self-switching**
   - Allow switching only among explicitly allowlisted models.
   - Optional per-session or per-job scope only.
   - No open-ended autonomous model selection.

3. **Quota-aware degradation only**
   - Restrict the feature to downgrade/fallback behavior on hard failure conditions, not general task-complexity routing.

## Why this differs from #16525

Issue #16525 asked for a general-purpose agent-callable `model_switch` tool based on task complexity.

This issue is narrower:
- focus on **recovery from hard model unavailability**
- bounded by **explicit allowlists / existing fallback policy**
- aimed at **unattended reliability**, not open-ended self-directed routing

## Why this matters

Without this, unattended workflows fail in exactly the cases where fallback matters most:
- cron jobs
- background agents
- overnight processing
- multi-profile deployments sharing account-level quotas

Today the workaround is external monitoring plus manual intervention. That is operationally brittle.

## Possible implementation directions

- Extend the existing fallback provider/model machinery so the **main agent** can inherit a bounded fallback chain on specific hard-failure classes.
- Or add a restricted internal retry path for the current session/job using a configured allowlist.
- Or expose a very limited switch primitive that is only callable under failure conditions and only toward pre-approved targets.

## Reference

Related rejected issue: #16525

That issue appears to have been rejected because it was too broad. This request is the narrower operational version: keep autonomous workloads alive when the chosen model becomes unavailable.

items.title: Gateway auto-reset banner reports base-config model/provider instead of active profile's
items.body:
## Summary

The **auto-reset notification banner** posted by the gateway (`◐ Session automatically reset … Model: <x> / Provider: <y> / <ctx> tokens`) reports the model, provider and context length from the **base config** (`~/.hermes/config.yaml`) instead of the **active profile's config** (`~/.hermes/profiles/<name>/config.yaml`).

Result: a session that is actually running on the profile's model shows a misleading banner advertising the base-config model. Cosmetic (the live session uses the correct profile model), but confusing when base and profile diverge.

## Environment

- Hermes v0.18.0 (editable install)
- macOS
- Multi-profile setup; gateway multiplexing profiles
- Base config `model.default: deepseek-v4-flash`, `provider: custom`
- Profile `planner` config `model.default: claude-opus-4-8`, `provider: anthropic`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run the gateway serving a non-default profile whose `config.yaml` overrides `model` / `provider`.
2. Let a session auto-reset (idle / daily schedule), so the reset notice fires.
3. Observe the appended session-info block: it shows the **base** config's model/provider/context, not the profile's.

## Root cause

In `gateway/run.py`, the reset notice appends `self._format_session_info()` (line ~10537). `_format_session_info()` (def at ~11773) resolves the model via:

```python
model = _resolve_gateway_model()      # -> _load_gateway_config()
...
data = _load_gateway_config()         # reads _hermes_home / 'config.yaml'  == BASE config
provider = model_cfg.get("provider")  # from base config
```

Both `_resolve_gateway_model()` (~2306) and `_load_gateway_config()` (~2212) read `_hermes_home / 'config.yaml'` — the **base** home — with no notion of the per-source profile.

Meanwhile the codebase already has all the machinery to do this correctly:

- `_resolve_profile_home_for_source(source)` (~16163) → resolves the profile `HERMES_HOME` for an inbound source.
- `_load_profile_config(profile_home)` (~2273) → loads a given profile's `config.yaml`.
- `_profile_runtime_scope(profile_home)` (~1372) → context manager that overrides `_hermes_home` for the duration of a block.

`_format_session_info()` simply doesn't participate in profile scoping — it's called outside any `_profile_runtime_scope` and hardcodes base-config reads.

## Suggested fix

Make `_format_session_info()` profile-aware. Either:

1. Have it accept an optional `profile_home` / `source` and resolve model/provider/context via `_load_profile_config(profile_home)` (falling back to base), **or**
2. Call it inside a `with _profile_runtime_scope(self._resolve_profile_home_for_source(source)):` block at the reset-notice site (~10537), so the existing `_load_gateway_config()` reads pick up the profile's `_hermes_home`.

Option 2 is the smaller diff and reuses the existing scoping helper. The auto-reset notice site already has `source` in scope.

## Impact

Cosmetic only — the live session runs on the correct profile model. But the banner misreports it, which is misleading in exactly the multi-profile scenarios the notice is meant to inform.

items.title: fix(desktop): switching chat session triggers auto-speak of the new session's last reply
items.body:
## Bug Description

When the "Read replies aloud" (auto-TTS) toggle is enabled in the desktop composer, switching to a different chat session **automatically triggers and reads aloud** the last assistant reply of the newly-selected session. The expected behavior is that session switching should be silent — audio should only play for *new* replies that arrive after the switch.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable "Read replies aloud" in the desktop composer (the speaker icon toggle)
2. Send a message in Session A → reply gets read aloud normally
3. Switch to Session B (with existing replies) via the sidebar
4. **Observe**: Session B's last assistant reply starts being read aloud automatically
5. Switch back to Session A → Session A's last reply also starts reading

## Expected Behavior

Switching between chat sessions should **not** trigger any TTS playback. Auto-TTS should only respond to replies that complete **after** the toggle was enabled and **after** the current session was entered.

## Root Cause Analysis

The issue is in `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-auto-speak-replies.ts` (added in PR #55154, merged 2026-06-29).

The `useAutoSpeakReplies` effect subscribes to the global `$messages` nanostore with `sessionId` as a dependency. When the user switches sessions:

1. The session switch code calls `$messages.set(newSessionMessages)` — this **synchronously** invokes all subscribers, including the old effect's `speakLatest` callback
2. React's effect cleanup (which unsubscribes the old listeners) **has not run yet** — it happens during the commit phase, which is after the nanostore update
3. `speakLatest` calls `pendingReply()` which reads `$messages.get()` — already the new session's data — and returns the new session's last assistant message
4. `playSpeechText(...)` is called, starting playback
5. Only then does the effect cleanup run, unsubscribing the stale listener — too late

The guard on line 52 (`latest.current.markSpoken()` in the effect body) is meant to consume the existing last reply when `sessionId` changes, but it runs **after** the stale subscription callback has already fired.

## Technical Details

- **File**: `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-auto-speak-replies.ts`
- **Introduced in**: PR #55154 (merged 2026-06-29)
- **Core mechanism**: `$messages.subscribe(speakLatest)` fires synchronously on store update, before React cleanup of the old effect
- **Related PRs**: #43845 (alternative auto-TTS, still open), #46672 (config-based auto-speak, also mentions session-switch trigger fix but uses a different mechanism, still open)

## Suggested Fix Direction

The simplest fix in `useAutoSpeakReplies`: add a check in the effect cleanup that stops any in-flight playback, and/or use a closure-scoped flag so `speakLatest` can detect it was called from a stale subscription during a session transition.

## Environment

- Hermes Desktop (main branch, post-PR #55154)
- Windows 10 confirmed; likely cross-platform

items.title: UX: model drift guardrail silently breaks all unpinned cron jobs on model change
items.body:
## Problem

When the global default model is changed via `hermes config set model`, ALL unpinned cron jobs silently fail on their next run with:

```
RuntimeError: Skipped to prevent unintended spend: global inference config drifted
since creation (model 'old-model' -> 'new-model'), and this job is unpinned.
```

Reference: #44585 (the drift guardrail)

## Impact

- Every unpinned LLM-based cron job is blocked until manually re-pinned
- No warning at config-change time — discovered one job at a time over hours/days
- In our case: 34 jobs broke simultaneously (drains, health checks, briefings, monitors)
- Each requires a manual `cronjob action=update job_id=X model=Y provider=Z` call

## Current Behavior

1. User runs `hermes config set model new-model`
2. No warning about affected jobs
3. All unpinned jobs fail on next run with RuntimeError
4. User discovers failures one at a time via error logs or missed deliveries
5. Must manually pin each job individually (34 separate commands in our case)

## Expected Behavior (any of these would help)

1. **Warn at config-change time**: `hermes config set model X` should report:
   ```
   WARNING: 34 unpinned cron jobs will be affected by this change.
   Run 'hermes cron pin-all --to-current-model' to update them, or they will be blocked on next run.
   ```

2. **Bulk-repin command**: `hermes cron pin-all --to-current-model` that updates all unpinned jobs in one shot

3. **Auto-repin with confirmation**: After model change, prompt:
   ```
   34 unpinned jobs were created under the old model. Update them to the new model? [Y/n]
   ```

4. **Softer failure**: Instead of blocking entirely, log a warning and proceed (with a config option to opt into strict mode)

## Workaround

We created a script that bulk-pins all unpinned jobs: `~/.hermes/scripts/pin-cron-jobs-to-current-model.py`

But this shouldn't be necessary — the CLI should handle this natively.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent version: latest (commit 605727e3b)
- OS: Linux Mint
- Model change: xiaomi/mimo-v2.5-pro -> xiaomi/mimo-v2.5

## Additional Context

The drift guardrail's INTENT is correct — prevent accidental spend on a more expensive model. But the UX of silently breaking all jobs is painful. A model change is a deliberate action; the system should help the user update their jobs, not punish them for forgetting.
